articles.title: Heatbit's $899 Water Heater Element Mines Bitcoin While It Heats Your Tank - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Heatbit has unveiled Bitwater, a water heater element with 20 Bitcoin mining chips that screws into existing electric tanks in the U.S. and Canada.
- The element produces up to 34 TH/s on up to 600 watts, and the first batch costs $899 to preorder, with later batches priced at up to $1,299.
- Heatbit pitches it as a way to decentralize Bitcoin mining, saying homes use more electricity heating water than the whole Bitcoin network does.
Heatbit, which makes space heaters with built-in Bitcoin miners, has unveiled a water heater element that mines Bitcoin while it heats water, the company said in a tweet on Thursday.
The element, called Bitwater, replaces the resistance wire in a standard electric water heater element with 20 Bitcoin mining chips, so the heat they give off warms the water instead. "Same heat, same electricity, plus bitcoin," Heatbit wrote, arguing that "the electricity was going to be spent on hot water anyway."
Introducing Bitwater: the water heater element that mines Bitcoin.
It screws into the electric tank you already have.
Physically decentralized mining that runs no matter what 🧵
Heat water. Mine Bitcoin. Same tank. pic.twitter.com/pRdxPbmpXM
— Heatbit (@heatbit_com) October 22, 2026
The element uses 20 of Bitmain's BM1370 chips and is rated at up to 34 terahashes per second, drawing up to 600 watts at an efficiency of 12 joules per terahash. The water cools the chips, so there are no fans and no noise, according to the company.
Heatbit describes installation as a do-it-yourself job: switch off the breaker, drain the tank, unscrew the old element and thread in Bitwater using an included wrench. It fits the standard one-inch port on regular 30- to 80-gallon electric tanks in the U.S. and Canada, including those made by A. O. Smith, Rheem, Bradford White, Whirlpool and GE, Heatbit said in a follow-up tweet, with no plumbing changes or new circuit needed.
At up to 600 watts, Bitwater draws far less power than the 4,500-watt elements common in U.S. tanks. Those heat water fast and then shut off, while Bitwater heats more slowly and runs for longer, Heatbit explained. When demand spikes, the tank's existing upper element still provides backup.
Users can track water temperature, hashrate and earnings in an app and choose between solo mining and joining a pool, with mined Bitcoin going to an address they control.
Preorders for the first production run, which Heatbit calls its "Genesis batch," cost $899, with later batches priced at up to $1,299. The refundable preorders are due to ship in the first quarter of 2027. Heatbit said it tested the element through the winter with households of four and five in New York and Florida, and teased a product for homes with gas water heaters.
Heatbit has not published its own earnings estimate. Instead, it shared a reply from xAI's Grok chatbot putting earnings at about $1 to $1.25 a day, adding that "estimates aren't guarantees." That is in line with Decrypt's own figures. At the current hashprice of about $36.73 per petahash per second per day, according to Hashrate Index, an element running at its full 34 TH/s would mine about $1.25 worth of Bitcoin a day, or roughly $455 a year. Heatbit says the element is built to run more than 80% of the time, and earnings would rise and fall with Bitcoin's price and network difficulty.
Heatbit's home mining pitch
Heatbit is pitching Bitwater as a way to spread Bitcoin mining across homes. Homes worldwide use about 300 terawatt-hours of electricity a year heating water, compared with about 170 terawatt-hours for the entire Bitcoin network, the company said.
"Public miners are fleeing to AI and dumping coins to pay Wall Street and CEO salaries," Heatbit wrote. "Home miners answer to no one."
Large public miners have been moving into AI. Bitcoin miners struck 17 deals worth more than $110 billion over two years, contracting out roughly 6 gigawatts of power to companies including Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Nvidia and CoreWeave, Bernstein said earlier this year. The bank expects AI revenue at the miners it covers to grow from $1.2 billion in 2026 to $10.7 billion by 2030, and has said the sector's planned power capacity of more than 27 gigawatts makes miners key suppliers for the AI boom.
The two businesses work differently, though. Bitcoin miners can switch off to relieve pressure on the grid, while AI data centers need power around the clock. "We're interruptible [as Bitcoin miners], whereas a traditional data center needs (to be) on 100% of the time," Shanon Squires of Compass Mining told Decrypt in March 2025.
The company's first product, a space heater with a built-in miner, cost almost $700 in 2023. Founder Alex Busarov told Decrypt at the time that it would always earn something however mining economics changed, because the heat it produced was replacing a conventional heater's. "Dyson doesn't make you any money. This one does," he said.

articles.title: UK's FCA says crypto apps may need licenses when algorithms choose trade routes
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The FCA says UK crypto apps may need licenses if their algorithms select trading venues or execution routes for customers.
- The proposal could bring DeFi aggregators and automated trading interfaces under Britain's incoming 2027 regulatory framework.
- Firms face uncertainty over licensing requirements as the February 2027 application deadline approaches before final guidance is assured.
Britain's financial watchdog warned that crypto trading apps could need regulatory approval if their software decides customer transactions.
In draft guidance published Oct. 21, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said applications that select trading venues or transaction routes based on assessments of price, liquidity, costs or execution speed may be arranging crypto deals, an activity requiring authorization under rules taking effect in October 2027.
The interpretation could bring decentralized finance (DeFi) aggregators and automated trading interfaces within the UK's licensing regime, potentially forcing operators to obtain regulatory permission or change how their software handles customer trades.
The proposal forms part of the FCA's efforts to define which crypto businesses qualify for exemptions from the new framework, scheduled to take effect on Oct. 25, 2027.
DeFi trading algorithms face licensing scrutiny
The FCA's consultation focuses on a technical-services exemption intended to protect software providers whose applications simply connect customers to third-party trading platforms or decentralized protocols.
Under the proposed interpretation, an interface that transmits customer instructions without influencing their execution may qualify for the exemption.
However, applications that evaluate competing liquidity sources, recommend trading venues, or determine how transactions are executed could be performing activities that require regulatory authorization.
That distinction matters for DeFi aggregators, which often compare prices and liquidity across decentralized exchanges to identify execution routes for customers.
The regulator identified several indicators of discretionary involvement, including modifying transaction instructions, determining execution timing and selecting routes based on counterparty risk or expected trading outcomes.
Applications promising customers the best available execution may also face greater scrutiny because such commitments can indicate that their operators are making judgments about competing trading options.
The FCA further warned that automating these decisions does not necessarily shield developers or operators from regulation. Algorithms can execute choices established by their providers, including criteria that determine which exchanges or liquidity sources receive customer orders.
The assessment would therefore extend to how trading software is designed and operated, even when individual transactions are completed without direct human intervention.
Still, the regulator's interpretation leaves room for applications using predetermined, objective routing rules. Whether a provider exercises discretion is one consideration alongside its broader involvement in facilitating transactions.
The exemption also carries separate eligibility requirements, including restrictions on authorized firms and payment service providers. It applies to qualifying technical access arrangements rather than every software service connected to decentralized finance.
The proposals extend beyond trading interfaces to the operators of decentralized platforms.
The FCA said distributed governance, smart contracts and automated systems do not automatically eliminate regulatory obligations where identifiable individuals or businesses exercise control over services.
Its assessment will consider operational responsibilities, decision-making authority and economic interests when determining whether an entity carries out regulated activities.
Those provisions could complicate compliance arrangements for DeFi businesses whose developers, governance participants and commercial operators share responsibility for maintaining trading infrastructure.
The uncertainty comes as the FCA's authorization window is already open. Existing UK crypto businesses seeking transitional protections must submit applications between Sept. 30, 2026, and Feb. 28, 2027.
The regulator has requested feedback on its proposals by Nov. 18. Its website targets January 2027 for final guidance, although the consultation paper identifies spring 2027, potentially leaving affected businesses with limited time to determine their licensing requirements.
Acknowledging the uncertainty, the FCA said it may grant additional time to complete arranging-permission details where the proposed technical-services exemption materially affects an application. Businesses must still submit otherwise complete applications within the prescribed window.
Affected operators can also seek pre-application support from the regulator, which can help them assess their transaction-routing systems and determine whether they need to change their operating models or authorization applications before the February deadline.

articles.title: Bitcoin in 'Wait and See Mode'—And That Might Be a Good Thing - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin hasn't moved more than 6% over the past month, and every top five cryptocurrency has failed to move more than 2% over the past seven days.
- Market analysts say that a boring market isn't a bad sign, that it could actually be an early sign of an incoming bull market.
- One expert says Bitcoin is in "wait and see mode," as investors wait for the Federal Reserve's rate decision on October 28.
Bitcoin hasn't budged more than 6% over the past month, per Decrypt data, and is currently sitting at around $81,735, down 1.2% on the day. One expert says the leading cryptocurrency is in "wait and see mode," and claims that might be a good thing.
The crypto market as a whole has been quiet lately. Every top five cryptocurrency has failed to move more than 2% over the past week. And the Crypto Fear and Greed Index is at a neutral score of 47. It's all quite… boring.
But market analysts say that a dull market might actually portend a bull market, and that there are still opportunities out there.
A quiet market is "usually a good sign, and one reason is that it doesn't last," Jake Koch-Gallup, senior research analyst at Blockworks, told Decrypt. "In the past, similar low-volatility stretches have led to 30% price swings in either direction within a few months."
André Dragosch, head of research at Bitwise Europe, called the quiet period a "constructive sign." That's because "long stretches of uneventful trading punctuated by a handful of outsized moves" is a typical early sign of a bull market.
The drawdowns in Bitcoin's current recovery have also been less damaging than in previous cycles, Dragosch said. That's all while oil, semiconductor stocks, and government bonds are experiencing "elevated" volatility, he added.
"That tells us investors are increasingly willing to absorb weakness and maintain exposure," Dragosch told Decrypt, calling it "resilience rather than euphoria."
Conversely, Carlos Guzman, vice president of research at crypto trading firm GSR, told Decrypt that a boring market isn't either a good or a bad sign. Rather, he said, the market is standing still due to a "risk-off" sentiment taking over global markets.
"This has been mostly due to factors outside of crypto, with a complex macro situation and fears around AI stocks taking center stage," Guzman said. "We're unlikely to see a significant market breakout while broader risk-off sentiment prevails, so markets continue to be choppy."
'Wait and see mode'
Dragosch told Decrypt that Bitcoin is in "wait and see mode," with markets stuck between tightening global financial conditions and an expectation that slowing growth will eventually force central banks to change course.
Mostly, what Bitcoin is waiting for is the Federal Reserve. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time since 2023, and CPI then rose 0.6% for September. The Fed's next rate decision is on October 28, "and until then nobody wants to make a big bet," Koch-Gallup said.
Bitcoin is hovering around what Dragosch calls "the market's economic midpoint," the level where roughly half of all invested capital is in profit and half is at a loss. That means "neither buyers nor sellers currently have much incentive to move the market away from this level," he said.
That doesn't mean nobody is buying. Bitcoin briefly dipped below $80,000 last week but "quickly found buyers," Guzman said, and BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF saw an inflow of $665.20 million on Monday, according to CoinGlass data.
"The problem is that buying hasn't been consistent enough to drive a sustained rally," Guzman said.
The next move
Koch-Gallup said three catalysts are coming in the next two weeks: the Fed decision on October 28, an options expiry on October 30 of $11.69 billion worth of Bitcoin, and the U.S. midterms on November 3. These events could dictate the crypto market's next major move.
"If the Fed keeps rates the same and ETF inflows keep coming, I'd expect the break to be upward," Koch-Gallup said. "If the Fed hikes again, the $75,000 to $77,000 floor comes back into play."
Plus, Guzman added that a resolution to tensions around the Strait of Hormuz could also act as a catalyst for markets.
Dragosch said derivatives markets are pricing in far less volatility than on-chain data suggests, which means options are "unusually cheap right now, both for hedging and for positioning for a larger move in either direction."
"For me, a boring market is the time to buy high-quality protocols before a bull market makes them overvalued," Koch-Gallup told Decrypt. "I'm focused on revenue-generating businesses with strong tokenholder claims."
While Bitcoin and other major tokens have traded sideways, smaller coins have made moves.
Brave browser token BAT has climbed almost 87% to a $263 million market cap over the past month, according to Decrypt data, while card collection marketplace Collector Crypt has jumped 95% to $318 million.
"A boring market means you have to work harder to find the opportunities, not that they aren't there," Koch-Gallup said.

articles.title: Switzerland Approves First Retail Spot Bitcoin ETF
articles.text:
Switzerland’s first retail spot Bitcoin ETF targets November launch
BIT Asset Management’s Bitcoin Fund ETF is expected to begin trading on SIX Swiss Exchange in November, with its public offering restricted to Switzerland.
Switzerland’s financial regulator FINMA’s first approved spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund for retail investors is expected to begin trading in November.
On Tuesday, FINMA announced it had approved the country’s first spot Bitcoin ETF that invests directly in Bitcoin, but did not disclose who the issuer was.
On Thursday, BIT Asset Management said its Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT) is expected to begin trading on SIX Swiss Exchange next month. The fund holds Bitcoin directly and is approved for public offering in Switzerland only.
“Most bitcoin products listed in Europe today are exchange-traded products (ETPs), which are debt instruments that carry issuer risk,” said BIT Asset Management.
The Bitcoin Fund ETF is instead a Swiss collective investment scheme, where assets are held separately from those of the fund management company and are “ring-fenced” for investors, it said.
The fund falls under Switzerland’s “other funds for alternative investments” category with particular risk. FINMA noted that other fund providers have also submitted applications for Bitcoin ETFs.
While FINMA has allowed funds that invest primarily in a basket of cryptocurrencies since 2021, this is the first time that FINMA has approved a fund that only invests in Bitcoin, citing trading history and higher trading volume compared with other cryptocurrencies.
However, it stressed that Bitcoin remains highly volatile even when accessed through an approved ETF.

articles.title: SpaceX perpetual futures traded about $6 billion after earnings
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Talos reported about $6 billion in SpaceX perpetual turnover across Binance and Hyperliquid after earnings, over eight times the prior day.
- Talos reported Binance open interest fell about 8% after earnings, even as SpaceX-linked perpetual trading surged.
- Fees depend on the venue, trader tier and market settings. Hyperliquid's assistance fund converts its own receipts to HYPE and burns the tokens.
SpaceX perpetual futures trading surged around the company’s October 20 earnings release, even as Binance’s outstanding dollar exposure fell, according to market-data provider Talos.
Talos’s October 22 report puts SpaceX perpetual turnover across Binance and Hyperliquid at about $6 billion in the post-earnings episode it describes, more than eight times the prior day’s volume. Talos also reported that Binance open interest fell about 8% after earnings.
The figures separate trading activity around earnings from exposure left open afterward. Executions can create fee opportunities even while outstanding exposure contracts.
SpaceX’s third-quarter results release scheduled its earnings call for 4:30 p.m. Eastern on October 20. Talos says Binance’s SPCX perpetual gained 8.5% from the earnings print to the following US open.
The turnover figure covers two venues, while the dollar-open-interest figures are Binance’s alone. The two measures have different venue coverage and time windows, limiting comparisons between the trading surge and the positions that remained open.
How SpaceX perpetual futures generate fees
Volume and open interest measure different activity. Volume counts contracts traded during a period. Open interest counts contracts that remain outstanding, with each buyer-and-seller pair counted once.
Consider an existing long who sells to an existing short buying back to close. The execution adds volume, while both positions close and open interest falls. A busy market can therefore finish with fewer contracts outstanding.
Hyperliquid’s initial-margin formula multiplies position size by mark price and divides by leverage. Shared collateral and unrealized profits can affect margin available for other positions.
The current SPCX specification from market operator trade[XYZ] references one SpaceX Class A share quoted in dollars and permits cross margin with maximum leverage of 20 times.
These are derivative positions referencing the share’s price. Perpetual contracts use funding payments designed to help align their prices with the underlying in contracts with no scheduled expiry. The notional value of trading those contracts is consequently a different measure from purchases of the underlying stock.
Closing trades can produce fees alongside declining open interest. Estimating the commercial result follows a separate chain: turnover at each venue, the effective net fees charged, and the amounts allocated to each recipient.
Under Hyperliquid’s HIP-3 framework, market deployers define contract specifications and oracles, set leverage limits and can settle markets while using HyperCore’s order books and margin infrastructure. Their individual settings help determine how trading becomes income for the operator and protocol.
Hyperliquid’s rates depend on rolling 14-day trading volume, maker or taker status, staking discounts and referral eligibility. Eligible makers can receive rebates. Different users can therefore generate different net fees on the same amount of turnover.
The trade[XYZ] fee schedule illustrates the scale of that difference. Its tier-zero base standard taker rate is 0.09%, compared with 0.009% under its growth-mode schedule. The corresponding maker rates are 0.03% and 0.003%.
Growth mode is conditional. Hyperliquid says activating it on an eligible HIP-3 market reduces fees, rebates and volume contributions by at least 90%, with other discounts also affecting the outcome. SPCX’s historical growth-mode setting and its October 20–21 mix of trader tiers and rebates remain unverified.
The division of fees matters too. trade[XYZ] describes its standard fees as split equally between Hyperliquid and the operator. Other HIP-3 deployments can have different fee settings.
Applying one displayed Hyperliquid rate to Talos’s combined-venue turnover would skip all of those distinctions, including the portion traded on Binance. The event’s actual retained fees remain unquantified.
What reaches HYPE
Hyperliquid’s fee-allocation rules direct fees to several recipients, including market deployers and its assistance fund. The documentation says HIP-3 deployers may keep up to half of trading fees generated by their assets.
The assistance fund automatically converts the trading fees it receives into HYPE, and the acquired HYPE is burned. The relevant channel for token holders is therefore the fund’s own receipts and conversions. Gross trading fees, operator receipts and funds reaching that mechanism are different amounts.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs shed $635 million as BTC tests their holdings’ estimated $81,500 cost basis
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin ETFs shed about $635 million on Oct. 22, their largest daily outflow since June, erasing nearly 60% of three days' inflows.
- Glassnode estimates an $81,500 cost basis for the Bitcoin held by US spot ETFs, near the latest pullback.
- Glassnode puts the next downside reference near $77,600 if Bitcoin closes below $80,000. The Fed's next decision is due Oct. 28.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded about $635 million in net outflows Thursday as the cryptocurrency traded near the estimated cost basis of the funds' Bitcoin holdings.
The Oct. 22 withdrawals were the largest daily outflow since June 25 and reversed nearly 60% of the inflows the funds attracted over the previous three trading sessions, per SoSoValue data.
BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led the selling with $254 million in withdrawals, followed by Fidelity's FBTC at $217 million. Together, the two funds accounted for approximately 74.2% of the day's net outflows.
ARK Invest's ARKB shed another $109 million, while Grayscale's GBTC and Bitwise's BITB lost $30 million and $27 million, respectively. Morgan Stanley's MSBT was the only fund to attract fresh capital, recording about $2 million in inflows.
The reversal coincided with Bitcoin's decline to as low as $80,841 during the reporting period, extending the cryptocurrency's struggle to recover as escalating Middle East tensions and renewed concerns about US technology stocks unsettled financial markets.
Bitcoin's institutional support faces pressure from rising oil prices
The latest withdrawals interrupted a recovery that had appeared to restore institutional demand following two consecutive weeks of ETF outflows.
Bitcoin funds attracted $527 million on Oct. 19, then $23 million on Oct. 20 and $528 million on Oct. 21. Thursday's selling reduced the week's net inflows to about $443 million.
Simon-Peter Massabni, head of business development at XS.com, told CryptoSlate that the unstable flows stem from increasingly cautious investors seeking short-term trading opportunities rather than committing capital for extended periods.
He said Bitcoin continues to find tentative support above $80,000, although buying momentum remains insufficient to establish a sustained recovery.
In its Oct. 21 market report, Glassnode estimated, using data through Oct. 19, that US spot Bitcoin ETFs acquired their holdings at an average price of approximately $81,500, while corporate Bitcoin treasuries hold their coins at an estimated average cost of $80,200.
The analytics firm found that buy orders around $80,000, substantially depleted during the Oct. 15 selloff, had been replenished by Oct. 20, although at smaller levels than previously recorded.
However, corporate treasury accumulation has weakened considerably, with monthly purchases remaining below one-tenth of their November 2024 peak since June. That has reduced another potential source of demand during market declines.
Glassnode identified the True Market Mean near $77,600 as the next major downside reference if Bitcoin closes below $80,000. Conversely, holders' acquisition costs and concentrated selling orders between $85,000 and $87,500 could limit any recovery.
Massabni warned that developments beyond the cryptocurrency market could further constrain investors' willingness to accumulate Bitcoin.
Escalating Middle East hostilities have raised concerns about energy supply disruptions, sending Brent crude above $110 a barrel and threatening to intensify global inflation pressures.
He argued that persistently elevated energy prices could force central banks to keep monetary policy restrictive, reducing liquidity available for speculative investments.
Pressure was also evident in US equities, with the Nasdaq Composite down 2.6% on Thursday and the S&P 500 down 1.21%, partly reflecting concerns about returns on heavy artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.
The Federal Reserve's next policy decision is due Oct. 28.
Ethereum ETF withdrawals deepen
Ethereum has faced a more sustained withdrawal of ETF capital, with US-listed funds recording about $111 million in net outflows on Oct. 22.
SoSoValue ETF flow data show BlackRock's ETHA lost $75 million, while its staking-focused ETHB product recorded another $17 million in withdrawals.
Grayscale's two Ethereum funds shed a combined $20 million. Fidelity's FETH attracted about $2 million, providing the only positive contribution among funds reporting activity.
The withdrawals brought Ethereum ETF losses to approximately $1,180 million in October, exceeding September's $832 million in inflows and reducing year-to-date net inflows to about $387 million.
Massabni observed that institutional demand for Ethereum remains inconsistent despite occasional positive flow sessions.
The funds lost a combined $129 million across Oct. 19 and 20 before attracting $15 million on Oct. 21. Even during that brief recovery, BlackRock's ETHA continued to experience withdrawals.
“One session of inflows is encouraging, but it is not enough to offset the preceding withdrawals,” Massabni said.
He added that Ethereum's price recovery would require several consecutive sessions of sustained buying, with the cryptocurrency struggling to establish a firm base around $2,400.
Bitcoin is -0.28% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #1 by market cap.

articles.title: Coinbase to drop this Japanese yen stablecoin years after its price crash sparked investor lawsuits
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Coinbase will automatically convert GYEN holdings into USDC from Oct. 26 as the $13 million stablecoin approaches its final shutdown.
- The closure follows years of controversy over GYEN's price collapse, which triggered investor lawsuits and a $6.75 million settlement.
- Coinbase's market-rate conversion could produce different payouts from the issuer's fixed-value redemption, which remains available until Nov. 11.
Coinbase will automatically convert customers' remaining GYEN holdings into USDC next week, ahead of the stablecoin issuer's final redemption deadline.
The crypto exchange said in an Oct. 20 notice that it will disable GYEN transfers on Oct. 26 and convert outstanding balances between Oct. 26 and Oct. 30 at prevailing market rates without transaction fees.
The decision comes as GMO-Z.com Trust Company winds down the Japanese yen-backed stablecoin, which has a market capitalization of approximately $13 million. Customers seeking to avoid Coinbase's conversion must withdraw their tokens before Oct. 26.
The shutdown marks the final chapter for a stablecoin whose troubled trading history triggered investor lawsuits and eventually resulted in a $6.75 million settlement earlier this year.
GMO Trust prepares final redemptions before November deadline
GMO Trust began winding down GYEN and its dollar-backed ZUSD stablecoin in May, suspending new issuance and initiating the voluntary dissolution of its New York-chartered trust company.
In an Oct. 20 statement, the issuer reminded holders that its 180-day redemption period closes on Nov. 11, giving them three weeks to exchange their tokens directly for the currencies backing them.
Under the arrangement, eligible customers can redeem each GYEN for one Japanese yen and each ZUSD for one US dollar without fees charged by GMO Trust.
However, the process requires an approved account, identity verification, and an eligible linked bank account. Customers must also meet minimum redemption thresholds of 100 GYEN or one ZUSD, while banks may impose additional transfer or foreign-exchange charges.
These requirements create different financial outcomes for holders using Coinbase and those redeeming directly with the issuer.
Coinbase will use the prevailing market price when converting GYEN to USDC, while GMO Trust guarantees the token's stated yen value through its direct redemption process. Customers could therefore receive different amounts depending on the prevailing trading price and exchange rate.
GMO Trust has warned that secondary-market prices may deviate from their intended pegs as circulating supply declines during the shutdown.
The issuer has also established a mandatory redemption process for eligible tokens remaining after Nov. 11.
Those holdings will be converted into USDC based on their stated redemption values, with GYEN's dollar equivalent determined using an exchange rate fixed on Nov. 12. GMO Trust expects distributions to be completed by the end of 2026.
The process is subject to supported blockchain networks, compliance screening and wallet compatibility. Holders whose wallets don't meet those requirements may not receive automatic distributions.
Coinbase customers will miss that later conversion process unless they withdraw their GYEN before the exchange's cutoff. The platform has also warned that deposits made after the conversion may be unrecoverable.
GYEN's troubled trading history
GYEN's shutdown follows years of controversy over the stablecoin's price stability and its handling by Coinbase.
The token faced major problems shortly after Coinbase began supporting it in November 2021, when its trading price surged far above the Japanese yen before collapsing.
As CryptoSlate reported in May 2022, investors sued Coinbase and GMO Trust, alleging that both companies misled customers about the stability of a token marketed as maintaining a one-to-one peg with the yen.
The complaint alleged that some investors bought GYEN at prices up to seven times its intended value before the token plunged about 80% in a single day.
Coinbase subsequently restricted trading, a decision plaintiffs argued prevented customers from selling their holdings and compounded their losses.
The dispute eventually moved into separate legal proceedings after a federal judge ordered arbitration of the claims against Coinbase in January 2023. The case against GMO Trust continued in federal court, where investors pursued claims under New York and California consumer protection laws.
In May 2026, a federal judge approved a $6.75 million settlement for eligible investors who lost money after buying GYEN while it traded away from its intended yen value.
The settlement resolved the litigation against GMO Trust without a finding of wrongdoing. The company had disputed the allegations, and the agreement did not resolve the separate claims against Coinbase.

articles.title: Evernorth’s $132 million funding option could buy more XRP while reducing XRP per share
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Evernorth’s October 19 effective registration covers public warrants that could raise $132 million if fully exercised for cash.
- A conditional common-pool model needs roughly 70% of gross exercise cash allocated to XRP at the dated $1.32 price.
- Actual XRP-per-share accretion still requires current ownership and holdings figures, cash exercise receipts and executed token purchases.
Evernorth’s newly effective public-warrant registration creates a potential $132 million funding route for the XRP treasury company. Whether that money increases XRP per share depends on how much additional XRP accompanies each new economic share. Issuing shares expands the ownership base, so XRP holdings must grow faster than that base for the ratio to improve.
A conditional model using its disclosed closing capitalization and 473 million-token treasury puts the break-even allocation at roughly 70% of gross exercise cash at the October 22 XRP price snapshot of $1.32. That is an illustration of the financing economics, rather than Evernorth’s verified current per-share figure: the actual threshold requires a current reconciliation of ownership, holdings and share changes.
The SEC notice records October 19 effectiveness. Actual exercise receipts and XRP purchases will determine the per-share outcome.
The funding route and its economic owners
The October 19 prospectus covers up to 11,499,992 Class A shares issuable through public warrants with an exercise price of $11.5. Full exercise for cash would generate $132,249,908 before costs. Evernorth receives no additional money when investors subsequently sell those shares.
The warrants’ contractual exercise period began at the October 9 business-combination closing, following an October 5 amendment. Cash exercise also requires an effective, current registration statement and a current prospectus. October 19 effectiveness is therefore distinct from the start of the contractual exercise period.
Management expects any net proceeds to support general corporate purposes and has broad discretion over their use. The filing specifies no mandatory XRP allocation. Exercises are unassured, and a cashless exercise where permitted would not deliver the $11.5 exercise price in cash.
CryptoSlate’s earlier coverage examined the conditions on Evernorth’s closing cash. The warrant route creates another funding possibility, but the same distinction between financing capacity and executed token purchases still matters.
Evernorth defines its primary performance measure as XRP attributable to the public parent, or Pubco, divided by outstanding Class A and Class C shares. Its structure also includes outside ownership in subsidiary Pathfinder Digital Assets. The token count must therefore match the economic ownership represented by the share count.
The prospectus gives a closing basis of 23,638,882 Class A shares and 31,392,746 Class C shares, totaling 55,031,628. It separately identifies 22,953,128 Company Units held outside Pubco that can be exchanged into Class A shares. Those outside units already carry economic interests in the subsidiary.
Simply dividing all consolidated XRP by the publicly traded Class A count would overlook both Class C shares and outside ownership. Adding Pubco-held subsidiary units again would create a different problem by counting the same economic interest twice.
The executed subsidiary agreement describes post-closing asset contributions and generally provides a corresponding unit for either an A or C share, subject to exceptions. Its publicly rendered member schedule does not establish the current unit count. A Class C-to-A conversion also does not create another economic share.
The denominator needs a consistent date. Evernorth corrected its delayed-funding share issuance on October 12 after a clerical error in its closing Form 8-K. The closing filing and later prospectus also give different A/C totals. Those differences cannot simply be added to the later total as new dilution.
The allocation hurdle at $1.32
Assume the stated 473 million XRP sits in one common economic pool, one subsidiary unit backs each A/C share, the 22,953,128 outside units participate on the same basis, and no later token or capital changes have occurred.
On that basis, 55,031,628 Pubco shares plus 22,953,128 outside units give 77,984,756 economic claims. Dividing 473 million XRP by that total produces approximately 6.07 XRP per claim. An ownership-adjusted Pubco numerator would produce the same ratio under those assumptions; assigning Pubco all the tokens while omitting outside claims would not.
Each additional cash-exercised warrant share needs about 6.07 additional XRP to preserve the modeled ratio, and more to increase it.
XRP market data displayed $1.32 at 12:21 UTC on October 22, alongside a 13.8% decline over 30 days. At that frozen execution price, 6.07 XRP costs about $8.01. That is 69.62% of the $11.5 gross cash received for a new warrant share, before fees and slippage.
At full covered cash exercise, approximately 70 million additional XRP would preserve the model’s starting ratio. The cost would be about $92 million at $1.32; increasing the ratio requires more tokens.
| Full cash-exercise scenario | XRP bought at $1.32, before costs | Result against modeled parity | 
|---|---|---|
| 50% of gross proceeds buys XRP | 50 million | Below parity | 
| 69.62% buys XRP, approximately | 70 million | Preserves the ratio, approximately | 
| 100% buys XRP | 100 million | Above parity | 
Every row assumes full covered cash exercise and purchases at the October 22 snapshot price, before costs.
Allocating half the proceeds to XRP would increase the absolute token treasury yet reduce XRP per economic claim in this model. Cash retained for expenses or other uses may still have business value, but it does not count as additional XRP in the token measure.
Spending choices determine the outcome
Evernorth has already described a broader treasury strategy. Its October 14 announcement named Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo as partners for intended fourth-quarter strategies involving its stated 473 million XRP treasury. The agreements remained subject to conditions and approvals.
Deploying existing tokens, acquiring additional tokens and generating future yield are different activities. CryptoSlate’s earlier analysis of the per-share strategy identified that measure as central; the warrant route now supplies a specific allocation decision to assess.
The October 19 prospectus and October 14 strategy announcement provide no post-effectiveness public-warrant cash-receipt figure or resulting XRP-purchase total.
A higher token ratio measures accumulation per economic share. Dollar net asset value and the equity price are separate outcomes. Cash, liabilities and the price of XRP also matter to dollar value. A falling XRP price makes a fixed cash sum buy more tokens, but does not by itself increase the number already held per share.
The next decisive disclosure is a matched set of figures: shares and outside units outstanding, XRP attributable to Pubco, cash exercises and net receipts, and additional XRP acquired. Until then, the $132 million headline describes capacity. The allocation and ownership figures determine how much of that capacity can improve the per-share result.

articles.title: What Is an Agentic Activities Launchpad? Inside AX1 Console 2.0
articles.text:
Crypto has spent years perfecting the launchpad. First came token launchpads, where anyone could create and list a token in a few clicks. Then, in 2024, agent launchpads arrived on Base, most visibly Virtuals Protocol, turning AI agents into tradable tokens.
AX1, a startup ecosystem on Base, is betting on a third kind. It has launched AX1 Console 2.0, which it calls an agentic activities launchpad. The difference is in what gets launched: not an asset, but an agent with a job to do.
Defining the category
AX1 defines an agentic activities launchpad as a product where people launch AI agents into work instead of launching tokens. Each activity is a quest: the agent pays for a service, gets a result, and the payment settles publicly onchain.
The model rests on x402, an open payment standard introduced by Coinbase in 2025 and now overseen by a foundation under the Linux Foundation. x402 lets software pay for a web request in USDC as part of the request itself, with no account and no API key. For a launchpad built around agents, that matters twice: the agent can pay for its own work, and every payment leaves a record on Base.
How it works
Console 2.0 is built so that a user never sees the plumbing. The entry quest, Verdict, takes three steps:
- Pick a token by name or ticker.
- Console creates an agent, covers its first runs and starts the quest.
- The agent settles the run through x402, scans the token's onchain activity and trading metrics and returns a verdict card ready to share.
Verdict is built as entertainment rather than trading guidance. It gives a second opinion with personality, never a buy or sell call. Every run earns points on a weekly contest board, and at the end of each week the top players share a prize pool. Prizes are paid in SPCXc, Coinbase's tokenized SpaceX stock on Base.
Version 2.0 is mostly about removing friction. Earlier versions asked users to set up an agent before doing anything with it. In 2.0, the agent and its starting balance are created the moment the first run starts. Also new: a footprint checker for any Base wallet, and Console running inside the Base App.
Payments, not emissions
The economics are deliberately plain. Console does not reward users with newly minted tokens. Activity is paid for in USDC, run by run, so the price of a run does not move with the market. A run costs 2 cents. The first few are covered by a starter credit, so a new user sees a result before deciding to put in any money.
Since paid quests went live on September 7, 5,669 agent wallets have paid for runs, and Console's transaction volume has reached 605,876 x402 payments. Of those wallets, 1,424 went on paying once their starter credit was used up. On x402scan, the public explorer for x402 payments, Console has been among the top five sellers by transactions and paying agents over the last 30 days, which places it among the leading x402 apps on Base. It is also listed in the x402 Bazaar on Coinbase Developer Platform. Because every run settles on Base, these figures can be checked onchain rather than taken on trust.
Why quests
An agent is only as useful as the task it is given. A quest packages the three things a task needs: a clear input, a price and a result someone wants to see. That packaging is what lets a person with no code and no wallet setup hand work to an agent in one tap, and it is the unit AX1 plans to scale. Verdict came first because it is the simplest version of that: one input, one payment, one result that fits on a card.
What comes next
Console's quest and campaign partners include sport.fun, Upshot, Clash of Coins and BlockRun, and AX1 plans to add quests from more partner apps on Base, so agents can take on jobs beyond Verdict. A partner quest turns an app's own product into a paid job for agents, priced per run and settled through x402 like Verdict. Head-to-head agent competitions are also on the roadmap. Alongside Console, AX1 runs AX1 Assay, a paid service in which people evaluate how agents behave onchain, built for companies whose agents already run in production.
Console 2.0 is live at console.ax1.vc.
About AX1
AX1 is a startup ecosystem on Base built for the agent economy. AX1 Console is where agents work, AX1 Assay is how their work gets proven, and partner apps bring the jobs.

articles.title: Tether’s own AI study shows when buying a laptop costs more than cloud tokens
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Tether joined Tenstorrent’s closed Series E, extending its AI infrastructure strategy without disclosing its individual investment.
- Under QVAC’s assumptions, dense-model capacity is 55 million tokens per working month, below the calculated Singapore cloud break-even.
- Existing device owners avoid a new purchase hurdle, while sustained users still need suitable models and enough usable throughput.
Tether’s October 20 announcement of an investment in AI computing company Tenstorrent extends CEO Paolo Ardoino’s push for user-controlled technology. Yet QVAC, the stablecoin issuer’s local AI platform, shows why buying a laptop will not save every user money.
The constraint is usage. In one dense-model scenario, QVAC’s estimated output over a working month falls short of the volume needed to cover a new machine’s assumed cost against cheap cloud access. Existing device owners face a different calculation because they have no new purchase to recover.
Tether announced its participation as part of its effort to give developers and businesses more control over computing. Tenstorrent said on October 19 that it had closed a $1.5 billion Series E at a $6.2 billion post-money valuation. Tether’s individual commitment was not disclosed.
A laptop needs enough work to cover its cost
QVAC’s October 12 cost study spreads a $2,399, 32 GB laptop purchase across four years, producing a monthly hardware charge of about $50. It estimates that dense Qwen3.8-27B can process about 55 million tokens in a 176-hour working month, with 94% input and 6% output. Tokens are the units of text a model reads and generates. The price and speed figures concern different machines: QVAC measured performance on a 36 GB MacBook Pro M5 Max, so the comparison is illustrative.
The study’s original open-cloud comparison puts break-even at roughly 90 million tokens. That exceeds its estimated working-month capacity for this model.
Current regional pricing changes the threshold. Alibaba Cloud’s Singapore international schedule, checked October 22, lists Qwen3.8-27B at $0.5 per million input tokens and $3 per million output tokens, before promotions or cache discounts.
CryptoSlate’s calculation using the study’s 94/6 mix gives a blended price of $0.65 per million total tokens: 94% of $0.5 plus 6% of $3. Dividing the rounded $50 hardware charge by that rate puts break-even at about 77 million tokens a month.
At 55 million tokens, the corresponding API bill would be $35.75. At 22 million tokens, it would be $14.3. If those monthly usage levels and API rates held for four years, the avoided bills would fall short of the assumed purchase price, before operating costs or any remaining hardware value.
This is an illustrative expenditure comparison. It assumes the local and hosted versions are suitable for the same work, without establishing equal output quality. It also excludes operating costs.
Alibaba lists different prices for Beijing and separate charges for cached inputs. A workload that qualifies for cheaper caching could reduce its cloud bill further; a different input/output mix would change the blended rate.
The 55 million-token estimate applies to QVAC’s particular model, configuration and 176-hour window. Running for more hours changes the available processing time, while actual work still has to fit the model’s capabilities.
QVAC’s faster Qwen3.6 35B mixture-of-experts scenario reaches an estimated 200 million tokens in the same working window. That could accommodate its illustrative 110 million-token coding workload, which exceeds the dense model’s estimate.
The study also uses a Mac Studio for its coding-agent cost example. Apple’s September 22 announcement lists the M5 Max desktop starting at $2,499, consistent with that sticker price.
The sypherin benchmark repository reports 36.8 generated tokens per second for dense Qwen3.8-27B on a 128 GB Ryzen AI MAX+395 system using FP4 weights and multi-token prediction. That first-person community test uses a different configuration from QVAC’s Mac, so it supplies a separate measurement with its own quality and hardware assumptions.
Who can recover the cost of local AI?
Owners of an adequate device have the clearest starting advantage. The purchase has already happened, so local AI does not need to recover a new laptop’s full price. Electricity and other operating costs remain, and the device still needs enough memory and speed for the work.
For someone buying solely for occasional AI use, the hurdle is higher. A fixed hardware cost continues during quiet months, while an API bill follows consumption. The 22 million-token example shows how substantial usage can still leave a cheap hosted model well below a new laptop’s monthly allocation.
Sustained agent users have a more plausible route to savings when a suitable model and a viable faster configuration process enough comparable work, or when less hardware cost needs to be allocated to AI. A fast model that requires more retries, or cannot handle the task, would not provide the same economic result as a more capable service.
The four-year allocation assumes the buyer uses the hardware over that period. Actual cost recovery depends on the spending it replaces. For a device already needed for other work, allocating the entire purchase to AI can overstate the additional cost of running a local model.
Ardoino’s argument includes benefits that a token-price table cannot fully capture. In QVAC’s October 21 account of his October 7 AMA, he advocates AI owned by its users while acknowledging that phones do not currently match frontier models. He also allows that the hardest scientific problems may remain in large data centers.
Local inference can keep a downloaded model available offline and reduce dependence on a provider’s continued service. Keeping prompts and files on a device can matter even when cloud tokens cost less. QVAC qualifies that privacy benefit: connected tools can still send data elsewhere.
CryptoSlate’s May 11 QVAC analysis explored the earlier tradeoffs around execution, capability and control. The October financing adds a hardware investment to that strategy, while the cost study exposes the conditions under which user ownership can also mean lower spending.
Tenstorrent says its new capital will support Galaxy server deployment, AI and CPU technology, and commercial expansion. Neither financing announcement establishes a QVAC product integration or a resulting reduction in users’ bills.
Using the checked Singapore rates and QVAC’s 176-hour dense-model example, break-even still lies beyond estimated capacity. A buyer in that scenario would need to value control and privacy alongside any token savings.

articles.title: Bitcoin's $80,000 recovery faces liquidity questions as Binance's Tether flows swing $14 billion
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Binance's USDT flows with Tether swung nearly $14 billion as its tracked Ethereum stablecoin holdings declined to $38.8 billion.
- The reversal raises concerns about shrinking crypto buying power as Bitcoin struggles to sustain a recovery around $80,000.
- Cross-chain transfers complicate the picture, leaving unclear how much of the outflow represents actual dollar redemptions.
Binance's stablecoin flows with Tether have reversed by nearly $14 billion, raising concerns about declining liquidity at the world's largest crypto exchange.
An Oct. 22 investigation by blockchain analytics firm Bitquery found that Binance-linked wallets transferred $23.1 billion in USDT to Tether during 2026 while receiving $15.6 billion, leaving a $7.5 billion net imbalance toward the issuer. That compares with a $6.4 billion net inflow during all of 2025.
The reversal coincides with a decline in Binance's tracked Ethereum stablecoin holdings from $43.9 billion in April to $38.8 billion on Oct. 22. The findings raise questions about how much buying power remains available on the exchange as Bitcoin struggles to regain momentum around $80,000.
Binance's shrinking reserves raise questions about where the money went
Binance accumulated substantial stablecoin holdings throughout 2025, with its identified Ethereum wallets reaching a record $45.6 billion in November, more than triple their October 2024 balance.
That accumulation has since unwound. Stablecoin holdings slipped to $39.5 billion by July before falling to their lowest level since September 2025 this month, suggesting a decline spread over several months rather than a single withdrawal event.
The movement was most pronounced in Binance's largest cold wallet, which held about $28 billion in USDT at its peak but carried$16 billion on Oct. 22.
However, two other cold wallets accumulated a combined $6.2 billion over the same period. Bitquery accounted for those internal transfers when calculating the exchange's aggregate holdings, separating movements between Binance-controlled addresses from the broader reduction.
The transactions with Tether offer another perspective on that decline.
During all of 2025, Binance sent $16.6 billion in USDT to Tether's treasury. The corresponding transfers during the first ten months of 2026 have already exceeded that total, reflecting a substantial increase in tokens returned to the issuer.
Most of this year's outgoing activity originated on Ethereum, which accounted for $19.6 billion of the transfers. Incoming USDT followed a different route, with $13.6 billion arriving on Tron.
The change suggests that part of Binance's treasury activity may involve moving stablecoins between blockchain networks.
Under Tether's issuance procedures, exchanges can return USDT on one network and receive equivalent tokens on another without reducing the overall supply. The issuer can also retain returned tokens in its treasury before reissuing or destroying them.
Those arrangements complicate Bitquery's interpretation of the transfers as evidence of capital leaving cryptocurrency markets. Although the transactions show a substantial shift toward Tether, they do not independently identify how much USDT was redeemed for dollars versus moved between networks.
This distinction has consequences for cryptocurrency demand.
Stablecoins provide much of the dollar-linked purchasing power used to trade Bitcoin and other digital assets. Actual redemptions that remove USDT from circulation can reduce that pool of capital, particularly if new issuance fails to replace the withdrawn funds.
However, Binance's declining wallet balances and its transactions with Tether measure different aspects of exchange activity. The former tracks USDT and USDC held in identified Ethereum addresses, while the latter captures USDT moving between the exchange and its issuer across Ethereum and Tron.
Neither measure establishes how much customer capital has permanently exited the market.
Bitcoin's recent weakness around $80,000 heightens the concern, as renewed buying demand could help determine whether the cryptocurrency stabilizes or extends its losses.
Further declines in Binance's holdings, particularly alongside a sustained contraction in circulating USDT supply, would strengthen the case that stablecoin purchasing power is weakening.
A recovery in deposits or fresh issuance would instead indicate that liquidity is returning, potentially restoring a source of demand that helped support cryptocurrency trading during Binance's earlier accumulation period.

articles.title: Giá dầu có thể gây hiểm hoạ chính trị, Tổng thống Trump càng gỡ càng rối
articles.text:
Chính quyền Mỹ đã đề xuất chi hàng tỷ đô la hỗ trợ nông dân, nới lỏng quy định với các tài xế xe tải, giảm nhẹ lệnh trừng phạt với nhiên liệu Nga và gây sức ép buộc các đồng minh châu Âu giải phóng nguồn dự trữ khẩn cấp.
Tuy nhiên, giá dầu diesel vẫn cao, khiến ông Trump chưa thể giảm nhẹ tình hình mà đảng của ông mong muốn, dù đã tiêu tốn nguồn lực chính trị và tài chính.
Đảng Cộng hòa đang nỗ lực bảo vệ thế đa số mong manh tại Quốc hội, trong bối cảnh mối bận tâm của cử tri là chi phí sinh hoạt cao. Theo một cuộc thăm dò do Reuters/Ipsos thực hiện trong tháng 10, gần 80% người Mỹ cho rằng ông Trump phải chịu trách nhiệm về tình trạng giá cả hàng hoá tăng.
Theo Cơ quan Thông tin năng lượng Mỹ (EIA), giá dầu diesel tại Mỹ tăng gần 10 cent/gallon trong tuần gần nhất, lên mức trung bình 6,28 USD/gallon. Mức tăng này đảo ngược xu hướng giảm trong 2 tuần trước đó, và đồng nghĩa với việc giá nhiên liệu tiếp tục duy trì gần mức cao kỷ lục.
Áp lực chính trị đặc biệt lớn tại các bang thuộc Vành đai nông nghiệp như Iowa và Kansas, những nơi vốn có truyền thống ủng hộ đảng Cộng hòa. Ở đó, chi phí nhiên liệu và phân bón tăng cao, hoạt động thương mại bị gián đoạn và hiệu quả kinh tế nông nghiệp suy yếu đã làm gia tăng sự bất mãn trong một bộ phận cốt lõi những người ủng hộ ông Trump.
Nhà lãnh đạo Mỹ đã quảng bá các giải pháp liên quan đến dầu diesel ở những cuộc vận động tranh cử trên khắp khu vực này.
Ông ký một sắc lệnh hành pháp ngay trên sân khấu tại Nebraska, để cho phép sử dụng dầu diesel nhuộm đỏ cho các phương tiện lưu thông trên đường cao tốc; công bố gói hỗ trợ nông nghiệp mới trị giá 8 tỷ USD tại cuộc vận động ở Kansas ngày 19/10.
Những biện pháp này cho thấy sự đánh đổi mà ông Trump chấp nhận để tạo ra sự giảm nhẹ trong ngắn hạn. Gói hỗ trợ mới tạo thêm áp lực lên chi tiêu liên bang, trong khi quyết định liên quan đến nhiên liệu Nga có thể giúp Mátxcơva có thêm nguồn lực cho chiến dịch quân sự ở Ukraine.
Việc gây sức ép buộc các đồng minh châu Âu giải phóng nguồn dự trữ khẩn cấp đã gây ra những bất đồng ngoại giao.
“Tổng thống có xu hướng xem nhẹ những tổn thất dài hạn để đổi lấy lợi ích trước mắt, và tôi hoài nghi liệu có thực sự xuất hiện bất kỳ lợi ích ngắn hạn nào hay không”, ông Chris Borick, chuyên gia thăm dò dư luận và nhà khoa học chính trị tại Đại học Muhlenberg, nói với Reuters.
Nhà Trắng cho rằng giá dầu diesel cao là do “những vấn đề đã tồn tại từ trước”, trong đó có tình trạng các nhà máy lọc dầu đóng cửa nhiều năm và thiệt hại do cuộc xung đột Nga – Ukraine.
Người phát ngôn Nhà Trắng Taylor Rogers cho biết: “Tổng thống muốn giá dầu diesel giảm xuống, đó là lý do ông đã thực hiện những hành động mang tính lịch sử nhằm giúp nông dân, tài xế xe tải và người lao động Mỹ tiết kiệm từng đồng tiền khó nhọc kiếm được”.
Đánh đổi nhiều thứ
Trong tháng này, ông Trump ký sắc lệnh cho phép tài xế xe tải sử dụng dầu diesel nhuộm đỏ - loại nhiên liệu thường dành cho các phương tiện và thiết bị hoạt động ngoài đường bộ, chẳng hạn như máy móc nông nghiệp, khi lưu thông trên đường cao tốc. Biện pháp này đồng thời cho phép tạm miễn trừ một số điều kiện liên bang về báo cáo thuế và lưu giữ hồ sơ.
Tuy nhiên, Sở Thuế vụ Mỹ (IRS) không xóa bỏ thuế liên bang với dầu diesel. Thay vào đó, cơ quan này chỉ tạm thời miễn trừ yêu cầu báo cáo liên quan và các khoản phạt đến hết năm, khiến các trạm dừng xe tải và nhà bán nhiên liệu vẫn chưa rõ họ phải tuân thủ những quy định nào.
Ông David Fialkov, nhà vận động hành lang cấp cao tại NATSO - hiệp hội thương mại đại diện cho các đơn vị vận hành trạm dừng xe tải lớn nhất tại Mỹ, cho biết các thành viên đánh giá cao nỗ lực của ông Trump trong việc giải quyết chi phí dầu diesel. Tuy nhiên, hướng dẫn thực hiện vẫn còn “mơ hồ” và tiềm ẩn quá nhiều rủi ro.
“Tôi thực sự không thấy việc sử dụng dầu diesel nhuộm đỏ có thể tạo ra tác động đáng kể đến giá dầu diesel”, ông Fialkov nói.
Ông Trump cũng đang chuyển sang sử dụng các khoản chi trả từ ngân sách liên bang để giảm bớt gánh nặng cho một số nhóm cử tri đang chịu ảnh hưởng nặng nề.
Các khoản chi trả của chính phủ cho nông dân dự kiến sẽ vượt 47 tỷ USD trong năm nay, bao gồm các khoản hỗ trợ hàng hóa nông nghiệp và 12 tỷ USD tiền hỗ trợ do thuế quan mà Bộ Nông nghiệp Mỹ (USDA) phân phối đầu năm.
Chương trình cứu trợ nông nghiệp trị giá 8 tỷ USD mới sẽ đẩy tổng số tiền hỗ trợ lên mức kỷ lục 55,4 tỷ USD, vượt mức cao nhất trước đó là 45 tỷ USD vào năm 2020, khi nông dân nhận được hỗ trợ trong đại dịch.
Các khoản chi trả này có thể giúp nông dân ứng phó với chi phí gia tăng và doanh số sụt giảm, nhưng không trực tiếp giải quyết những gián đoạn thị trường đang đẩy giá nhiên liệu và phân bón lên cao. Chúng cũng làm dấy lên câu hỏi về việc sử dụng tiền thuế của người dân để bù đắp thiệt hại cho các nhà sản xuất - những thiệt hại mà các tổ chức nông nghiệp cho rằng một phần do chính sách thương mại và đối ngoại của chính quyền.
Một số nỗ lực của ông Trump nhằm tăng nguồn cung dầu diesel phải đánh đổi bằng hệ quả địa chính trị.
Quyết định nới lỏng trừng phạt dầu diesel của Nga - vốn được thiết kế để hạn chế nguồn thu năng lượng của Mátxcơva - vấp phải chỉ trích từ cả 2 đảng tại Mỹ, đồng thời cũng gây hoài nghi về khả năng có thể giảm đáng kể giá nhiên liệu trong nước.
Ông Trump bảo vệ cách làm này, khẳng định đây là biện pháp cần thiết để đưa Tổng thống Nga Vladimir Putin trở lại bàn đàm phán nhằm kết thúc chiến sự Ukraine.
Trong bối cảnh những biện pháp can thiệp của chính quyền không thể kéo giảm chi phí nhiên liệu, ông Trump bị cho là đang đẩy trách nhiệm sang Ukraine và Tổng thống Volodymir Zelensky, thay vì cuộc chiến với Iran, trước thềm cuộc bầu cử ngày 3/11.
Các nhà phân tích cho rằng cuộc xung đột với Iran mới là yếu tố lớn khiến dầu diesel tăng vọt. Cuộc xung đột đã gây gián đoạn dòng chảy dầu mỏ toàn cầu và nguồn cung nhiên liệu tinh chế. Các cuộc tấn công của Ukraine nhằm vào các nhà máy lọc dầu Nga cũng góp phần thắt chặt nguồn cung, nhưng tác động đến giá cả có phần hạn chế hơn.

articles.title: Mọi ống kính đều hướng về Địch Lệ Nhiệt Ba
articles.text:
TPO - Địch Lệ Nhiệt Ba xuất hiện mở màn tại sự kiện Thịnh điển Vogue với nhan sắc lộng lẫy, lấn át hết mỹ nhân còn lại như Lưu Diệc Phi, Cổ Lực Na Trát, Bạch Lộc.

TPO - Đêm nhạc "Chạm Việt Nam 2'' mở cửa tự do, dự kiến đón hàng nghìn khán giả đổ về khu vực phố đi bộ Trần Nhân Tông để gặp gỡ và thưởng thức các giọng ca như rapper Pháp Kiều, CoolKid, Hà Myo, Ali Thục Phương, Xệ Xệ, Quinzel, Noah Quốc Anh, Nhật Phát, Chris V...

TPO - Dưới bàn tay tài hoa của đạo diễn Nguyễn Vinh Sơn, Đất Phương Nam trở thành bộ phim truyền hình kinh điển, làm lay động hàng triệu trái tim khán giả suốt 30 năm.
TPO - Lễ tang đạo diễn, NSƯT Nguyễn Vinh Sơn tổ chức tại nhà thờ ở TPHCM. Nhiều đồng nghiệp, học trò chia sẻ kỷ niệm được ông dìu dắt, trao cơ hội bước vào điện ảnh.
Trong 2 ngày 22 và 23/10, khu vực đổi vòng tay check-in cho concert BIGBANG 2026-2027 WORLD TOUR < XX : COSMOS > IN HANOI đã trở thành điểm hẹn sôi động của hàng chục nghìn người hâm mộ. Hoạt động này đánh dấu bước khởi động cho bầu không khí trước hai đêm diễn được mong chờ vào ngày 24 và 25/10 tại Sân vận động Mỹ Đình, Hà Nội.
Live concert “Bay về phía mặt trời” của ca sĩ Tùng Dương sẽ diễn ra vào ngày 19/12/2026 tại Sân vận động Mỹ Đình, Hà Nội, đánh dấu cột mốc 25 năm hoạt động nghệ thuật của một trong những tên tuổi hàng đầu nền âm nhạc Việt Nam. Đồng hành cùng chương trình với vai trò Nhà tài trợ Kim cương, Ngân hàng TMCP Quốc Dân (NCB) và Tập đoàn Sun Group góp phần tạo nên một sự kiện nghệ thuật chất lượng, nơi âm nhạc kết nối các thế hệ, tôn vinh bản sắc Việt và lan tỏa khát vọng vươn tới tương lai.
