articles.title: VCs, Superhuman Mail founder share red flags about product-market fit | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Product-market fit — when a startup’s product sells well — has become even harder to find in this AI era. Despite startups achieving record-fast growth, not all customers are sticky and products can be replicated more easily than ever.
Anu Bharadwaj, a partner at Iconiq; Rajeev Dham, a partner at Sapphire Ventures; and Rahul Vohra, the founder of Superhuman Mail, discussed the new rules for product-market fit last week at TechCrunch Disrupt.
“It’s never been easier to gain a bunch of pilots because lots of companies across the board are open to trying new things,” Bharadwaj said to the audience. “But going from pilot to production is really the hard thing.”
Right now, she said, a lot of founders pitch revenue metrics to investors without specifying which revenue they are talking about. “Is it true ARR or is it run rate?” she said. “There’s many ways to obfuscate the whole thing.”
Lately, much chatter on X has focused on AI founders inflating ARR numbers (which could mean “annualized run rate” or the more solid “annual recurring revenue”) to make it seem like their companies are doing better than they are. A common gimmick is counting pilot customers, who might only use the product for a couple of months, in the annualized run rate revenue number, implying that income is expected to continue for the entire year.
It should be obvious, but Bharadwaj pointed out, “It’s definitely in your long-term interest that you be very honest and upfront about what quality of revenue this is.”
She said companies need to separate hype from reality when looking at the quality of their revenue. It’s a red flag, for example, if only a few customers make up much of a company’s revenue or if the customers can easily go to another vendor for a better price. “Churn rate and retention [are] really dependent on that,” she continued.
That’s why Vohra advises startups to track customer engagement and dollar retention, especially for consumer products. “Figure out what benchmark [is] good, great, and excellent for your space,” he said.
For example, at Superhuman, he said that the company tracked ARR but also had their own internal metric called “delighted ARR,” which, he said, “was the ARR only from customers who are super engaged with the product.” He said that metric helped them see how sticky the customers were and how long they were likely to stay around.
“Those users are now still users, those companies are now still customers,” he continued. “We obsessed over serving that particular category of our user base and our customer base.”
The panelists also discussed green flags that indicate a startup has indeed found product-market fit. For Vohra, he said talk to customers to understand what value they find in the product and how they would feel if they could no longer use it. Then be honest with yourself when measuring those responses.
“If you’re 15%, 14%, 13%, or below, consider a complete pivot. Take the codebase, take the team, build something entirely new. “But if you’re 20%, you can totally optimize your way from 20% to 40%,” Vohra said.
Actually, Dham said, it’s important for a founder not to confuse having a vision with having a good business.
At the seed level especially, Barudvaj said that it’s fine to pivot. She doesn’t even look for product-market fit at that stage, but “does the founder have a thesis that seems plausible and do they have the agility to duck and wave as the situation changes?” she said.
Dham added that he values founders even more these days who have made numerous pivots because it shows they’ve had to make very hard decisions in this ever-shifting moment.
Product-market fit, therefore, is something founders will always have to redefine and re-earn. “Even at a billion in revenue, these companies are re-earning their product-market fit,” he said. “You constantly have to be innovating on products.”

articles.title: Could This Samsung Flip8 Be Your Last Chance to Snag a Small Foldable Smartphone?
articles.text:
Compact and lightweight. Top-notch performance. Solid main camera. Handy AI features.
TIRED
Price bump over last year. No telephoto camera. Cover screen is more useful but still limited.
If you crave a compact phone that doesn’t feel like a brick in your pocket and slips easily into a small bag, the flip style is for you. Samsung’s eighth-generation clamshell is seriously refined, and as svelte and slick as it comes. It may not offer a tablet-sized screen or the fashionable new passport shape, but it is arguably the most practical type of folding phone.
Like almost every other phone this year, the Z Flip8 offers tiny improvements over its predecessor and costs $100 more. If you’re wondering whether it’s worth updating from last year’s Z Flip7, it’s not. The Flip8 is a teeny bit lighter and slimmer with a newer processor, and that’s about it. But if you’re looking to dip a toe in folding-phone waters or just want something small, the Z Flip8 should be in the conversation.
Slimmer and More Foldable
Photograph: Simon Hill
Everyone is excited about the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8’s sexy new form factor, but Samsung continues to iterate on the flip phone format for folks who prize compact devices. The Z Flip8 shaves off 0.02 inches (0.55 millimeters) and a third of an ounce (8 grams) compared to its predecessor, making it the slimmest and lightest option in this category. The improved hinge makes the crease slightly less noticeable and a little easier to open. I still found it a bit tricky to open one-handed, but you get the knack after a while. The new hinge is also supposed to be more durable.
The Flip8 has an IP48 rating, so you don’t need to worry about dropping it in the bath, but tiny dust and dirt particles (less than 1 millimeter) can still cause damage. It comes in pink, like my review unit, as well as graphite, cream, and mint. It still has a physical SIM slot, and the power button has a fingerprint sensor in it that works pretty well.
The screens are the same as last year's. It has a sharp 4.1-inch AMOLED display on the outside with a 60- or 120-Hz refresh rate. Open it up to reveal the 6.9-inch main display, also AMOLED but with a variable refresh rate (1 to 120 Hz) that’s better for battery life. Both screens are reasonably bright (2,600 nits peak), and I never struggled to read the screen outdoors.
Powerful Performer
Photograph: Simon Hill
Flip phones used to get palmed off with lesser processors, but the Z Flip8 boasts the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy (the same cutting-edge chip that's in its two bigger siblings). It has 12 GB of RAM and 256 GB of storage. You can jump to 512 GB for an extra $200, but there’s no option to increase the RAM.
I encountered no stutters or lag and found performance to be generally excellent, whether jumping in and out of apps, firing up the camera, or gaming. The Z Flip8 can get warm, and this may throttle the processor somewhat if you’re playing a demanding game for a while (more than an hour). This is mostly down to the compact design.
The stereo speakers are better than I expected. They get quite loud without distortion, and they’ll serve you just fine for watching videos. Call quality is also solid, and slamming it shut to end a call never gets tired. I also like opening it to answer calls, but you must enable this in the Phone app settings under Flip options. Connectivity includes 5G (no mmWave), Wi-Fi 7, and Bluetooth 5.4, but there’s no ultra-wideband (UWB) for more precise positioning. The Fold8 models have Bluetooth 6 and UWB.
While it’s very capable, the Z Flip8 is only average when it comes to battery life, another drawback of its size. Samsung put in a 4,300-mAh silicon-carbon battery that’s good enough for casual use. If you’re on your phone a lot, you’ll want a power bank handy. Charging speeds are disappointing at 25 watts wired and 15 watts wireless, and I’m annoyed by Samsung’s refusal to implement the magnetic feature of Qi2.
Snap Shot
If you’re a keen photographer, you can get many better camera systems in a range of Android phones for the same money or less. That said, the main 50-megapixel shooter is perfectly good in many situations, and most folks will be happy with the photos it captures. Some noise creeps in when it’s dark. The 12-megapixel ultrawide is useful when you want to cram a lot in or take a group selfie, but it’s a definite step down in quality. Sadly, there’s no telephoto lens, but you can emulate 2X zoom without losing detail by cropping, and it offers passable results in good lighting up to 10X.
Photograph: Simon Hill
Samsung Galaxy Z Flip8, main camera.
I don’t see much reason to use the 10-megapixel punch-hole selfie camera outside of video calls, since you can flip it to get a cover-screen preview and use the main camera for selfies (a big benefit of this design). I also love Samsung’s Horizon Lock, which lets you shoot video with a steady horizontal plane no matter how you turn or move the phone.
Another new AI feature from Samsung is My FanCam, which lets you pick a subject to focus on in group videos and reframes them as though your chosen subject is the star. Handy for school plays or soccer games, if you remember to use it. (You can also apply it to old videos.) Speaking of AI, Samsung offers Now Brief to float up calendar events, reminders, and useful info like local weather, and Now Nudge to suggest adding dates to your calendar from messages, sharing locations or photos, and auto-filling forms.
Compact Competition
The cover screen, or FlexWindow, has been a weakness for Samsung’s Flip line, and it’s still limited in the Flip8. On the plus side, you can use more apps with the cover screen, including most of Samsung’s apps (Health, Calendar, Browser), YouTube, Netflix, Google Maps, and Messages. But if you want other third-party apps, you still have to install Good Lock, then the MultiStar plug-in, and select the apps you want to use. It’s stupidly convoluted, and I don’t understand why it isn't preinstalled, especially since Samsung has virtually all its other apps on there, along with a few third-party apps I never asked for (Facebook, Spotify, and Instagram). This is admittedly a bugbear of mine, but it's disgraceful that Samsung is including bloatware on a phone this expensive.
Photograph: Simon Hill
I like that you can have YouTube on the cover screen, as you can prop it up and there’s a little toggle at the bottom to switch between full screen, above the camera lenses, or standard vertical format for scrolling. You’ll mostly use the inner screen, but I have sometimes used the Flip8 this way to prop up a video I’m half-watching on my desk, and it’s a nice option to have.
There’s only really one competitor for Samsung if you’re set on a flip phone, and that’s Motorola's Razr line. You can step down to a less powerful but much cheaper Razr at $800, or spend a little more to snag the superior Razr Ultra. The latter has a better camera, more RAM and storage, and charges much faster, but it costs $1,500. The awkward middle child, the Razr+ at $1,100, is a tougher sell (it has an older processor and shorter software support). You might consider last year’s Z Flip7 if you can find it discounted.
Sadly, this might be your last chance to get a Samsung flip phone. Persistent rumors suggest Samsung will sunset this form factor as the Fold8 takes off and goes head-to-head with the iPhone Duo, though Samsung hasn't officially confirmed it. If you do pull the trigger on the Flip8, you get an excellent seven years of platform and security software updates, potentially taking you all the way to 2033. Who knows, maybe small phones will be back in fashion by then.

articles.title: Giá vàng hôm nay 23/10: Vàng nhẫn SJC giảm 1,3 triệu đồng/lượng
articles.text:
Giá vàng trong nước hôm nay 23/10
Tới 10h05' ngày 23/10, giá vàng miếng SJC niêm yết ở mức 139-142 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra), giữ nguyên so với mức mở cửa hôm nay.
Trong khi đó, giá vàng nhẫn loại 1-5 chỉ của SJC được điều chỉnh hạ xuống mức 135-139 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán), rẻ hơn 1 triệu đồng/lượng, nâng mức giảm từ đầu giờ sáng lên 1,3 triệu đồng mỗi lượng.
Giá vàng nhẫn của các thương hiệu khác cũng tiếp tục đi xuống. Giá vàng nhẫn 9999 tại Doji trưa nay giảm thêm 300.000 đồng mỗi lượng ở cả 2 chiều giao dịch so với mức niêm yết vào buổi sáng, xuống mức 137,7-141,7 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán). Tính từ sáng đến nay, giá vàng nhẫn 9999 tại Doji đã giảm 500.000 đồng mỗi lượng.
Tương tự, giá vàng nhẫn trơn của Bảo Tín Minh Châu trưa nay giảm xuống mức 137,4-141,4 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra), nâng tổng mức giảm từ lúc mở cửa lên 700.000 đồng mỗi lượng ở cả chiều mua và bán.
Mở cửa phiên giao dịch hôm nay (23/10), vào lúc 8h31', giá vàng miếng SJC được điều chỉnh giảm 300.000 đồng mỗi lượng ở cả chiều mua và bán so với mức niêm yết cuối phiên hôm qua, giao dịch ở mức 139-142 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra).
Giá vàng nhẫn loại 1-5 chỉ của SJC được niêm yết ở mức 136-140 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán), cũng giảm 300.000 đồng mỗi lượng ở cả 2 chiều giao dịch so với mức chốt của phiên giao dịch hôm qua.
Tương tự, giá vàng nhẫn 9999 của Tập đoàn Doji được điều chỉnh giảm 200.000 đồng mỗi lượng ở cả chiều mua và bán so với mức kết hôm qua, giao dịch ở mức 138-142 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra).
Giá vàng nhẫn trơn của Bảo Tín Minh Châu đầu phiên hôm nay cũng rẻ hơn 300.000 đồng mỗi lượng ở cả 2 chiều so với kết phiên hôm qua, niêm yết ở mức 137,8-141,8 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán).
Chốt phiên 22/10, giá vàng miếng SJC được niêm yết ở mức 139,3-142,3 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra), không thay đổi ở cả hai chiều so với chốt phiên giao dịch liền trước.
Giá vàng nhẫn loại 1-5 chỉ của SJC giảm 600.000 đồng/lượng ở cả hai chiều, xuống mức 136,3-140,3 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra).
Giá vàng nhẫn trơn tại Bảo Tín Minh Châu được niêm yết ở mức 138,1-142,1 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra), không thay đổi ở cả hai chiều.
Giá vàng thế giới hôm nay 23/10
Lúc 7h ngày 23/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá vàng thế giới giao ngay trên Kitco được niêm yết ở mức 4.020,3 USD/ounce (giá mua vào) và 4.022,3 USD/ounce (giá bán ra), giảm 3,8 USD, tương đương 0,09% so với mức tham chiếu của Kitco.
Lúc 21h30 ngày 22/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá vàng giao ngay ở mức 4.051 USD/ounce, giảm 91 USD. Giá vàng kỳ hạn tháng 12/2026 giao dịch quanh mức 4.068 USD/ounce.
Số liệu lao động Mỹ cho thấy thị trường việc làm duy trì ổn định. Số đơn xin trợ cấp thất nghiệp lần đầu trong tuần kết thúc ngày 17/10 giảm 6.000, xuống còn 194.000 đơn, thấp hơn dự báo 200.000 đơn. Dữ liệu này là một trong những yếu tố được thị trường cân nhắc khi đánh giá triển vọng chính sách tiền tệ của Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed).
Thị trường kỳ vọng Fed giữ nguyên lãi suất tại cuộc họp ngày 27-28/10. Trong khi đó, theo dữ liệu định giá thị trường được Reuters dẫn ngày 22/10, xác suất Fed tăng lãi suất 0,25 điểm phần trăm vào tháng 12 ở mức khoảng 86%. Giá dầu tăng cao khiến lo ngại lạm phát gia tăng, củng cố kỳ vọng Fed duy trì chính sách tiền tệ thắt chặt.
Lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc Mỹ kỳ hạn 10 năm giảm về gần 5%. Đồng USD vẫn tương đối mạnh, lãi suất duy trì ở mức cao, khiến kim loại quý kém hấp dẫn.
Căng thẳng tại eo biển Hormuz tiếp tục leo thang. Giá dầu Brent vượt 112 USD/thùng, mức cao nhất kể từ tháng 5. Dầu WTI tiến sát 100 USD/thùng. Giá năng lượng tăng làm gia tăng nguy cơ lạm phát toàn cầu.
Chứng khoán tại một số thị trường châu Âu và châu Á giảm trong phiên.
Trong những ngày tới, thị trường sẽ theo dõi các chỉ số PMI sản xuất và dịch vụ tháng 10 của Mỹ, cùng cuộc họp Fed ngày 27-28/10 và báo cáo lạm phát chi tiêu tiêu dùng cá nhân (PCE) ngày 29/10.
Dự báo giá vàng
Các chiến lược gia tại HSBC Asset Management cho rằng giá vàng vẫn có triển vọng tăng trong phần còn lại của năm 2026. Tuy nhiên, kim loại quý có thể tiếp tục đi ngang trong ngắn hạn do lợi suất thực duy trì ở mức cao và đồng USD mạnh lên.
HSBC cho rằng đà giảm của vàng trong thời gian qua chịu tác động từ giá dầu cao, lãi suất tăng và lợi suất trái phiếu đi lên. Ngân hàng này vẫn đánh giá vàng có vai trò quan trọng trong danh mục đầu tư. Căng thẳng địa chính trị, xu hướng đa dạng hóa dự trữ của các ngân hàng trung ương tiếp tục hỗ trợ nhu cầu.
Theo HSBC, lo ngại về nợ công và lạm phát có thể thúc đẩy dòng tiền chuyển sang các tài sản hữu hình như vàng. Hoạt động mua vàng của ngân hàng trung ương và dòng vốn ổn định vào các quỹ ETF cũng là những yếu tố hỗ trợ giá trong trung hạn.
Các chuyên gia HSBC cho rằng lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc Mỹ hiện là yếu tố quan trọng chi phối diễn biến giá vàng. Khi lợi suất tăng, chi phí cơ hội của việc nắm giữ tài sản không sinh lãi như vàng cũng tăng lên, khiến kim loại quý kém hấp dẫn hơn. Đồng USD mạnh cũng hạn chế đà tăng của giá vàng.
HSBC khuyến nghị nhà đầu tư không nên phụ thuộc vào một tài sản duy nhất để phòng ngừa rủi ro. Vàng vẫn có lợi thế nhờ tính thanh khoản cao và khả năng đa dạng hóa danh mục trong dài hạn. Tuy nhiên, nhà đầu tư cần kết hợp nhiều loại tài sản để ứng phó với những biến động khác nhau của thị trường.

articles.title: Split Tunneling Is Your VPN’s Best Feature. Here’s How to Make the Most of It
articles.text:
While you may well be familiar with virtual private network apps, you might not have come across one of the best features available inside these privacy protectors: a feature called split tunneling.
In simple terms, split tunneling lets you choose which apps or sites use the protection of a VPN and which don't. While VPNs are worth using for extra security and privacy online—foiling trackers, spoofing your location, and stopping your internet provider from seeing your browsing—they do by their nature come with some compromises in speed.
If, for example, you want to get the fastest possible speeds with your online games, you might want to leave your games outside of the VPN's remit. Likewise, since VPNs typically obfuscate your actual location, if you want to make sure you can always check movie showtimes in your local area, you can use split tunneling to keep those ticketing apps outside your VPN. Putting a VPN in place can also interfere with access to other devices on your local network, like smart home gadgets and printers.
For all these reasons, you might want the extra control that split tunneling gives you, and it's available in a lot of VPN packages. Here's what you need to know about it.
How VPN Split Tunneling Works
VPNs work by offering an encrypted bridge for data going to and coming from the web. This bridge means your internet provider, law enforcement agencies, and people connected to the same Wi-Fi can't see what you're doing online. Split tunneling lets you route some online traffic away from that bridge, without you having to constantly turn your VPN on and off.
App-based split tunneling is the most common type you'll come across, as it's the most straightforward and easiest to understand. Some of your apps use the VPN, and some don't. So maybe you want your banking app connected to a VPN for maximum protection, but you're less concerned about a weather app, and you don't want to see forecasts from whatever location the VPN is spoofing.
Depending on the VPN, you might also see URL-based split tunneling. This lets you set the rules based on domain names. It's the same idea as with apps: For websites that need fast internet access and where privacy is less important, there's no VPN. So you can keep the VPN turned on for a search engine page where you're typing information you want protected, but off for a local news site.
There are other types of VPN tunneling too, including route-based tunneling (based on specific IP addresses on the internet) and policy-based tunneling (essentially a set of overarching rules), but these are less common in consumer VPN software, and you're unlikely to come across them unless you're somehow managing other users.
It's not a complicated technology to understand, and it can be genuinely useful—but it's also a feature that users tend not to notice or think about when they're enabling and disabling VPNs on their devices.
How to Enable Split Tunneling
The exact steps needed to enable split tunneling will vary depending on the VPN software you're using, but they shouldn't be too difficult to find. Most, but not all, VPN programs now offer some kind of split tunneling feature. If you're using a popular app, then you should find the option somewhere, especially if you're on a paid tier.
To give you some idea how it works: In ProtonVPN for Windows, on the main console there's a split tunneling link on the right, together with other features like a kill switch and port forwarding. Click Split tunneling, and once it's enabled, you can start picking your apps. You can either select a list of apps to be included by the VPN (with everything else excluded) or a list of apps to be excluded (with everything else included).
For NordVPN on Windows, you can access the feature by clicking the cog icon in the bottom left of the main interface, then choosing Split tunneling and enabling the Split tunneling toggle switch. Again, you'll be able to choose which apps are included in the VPN protections and which ones aren't.
On mobile, it's a similar process: Delve into the settings for whatever VPN app you're using, wherever those settings might be. Note, though, that iPhones don't allow as much freedom for VPNs here as Android devices and desktop platforms: You'll typically be limited to selecting websites and IP addresses to exclude, rather than apps.
Most of the time, it's going to be a set-it-and-forget-it type routine, and you're not going to need to keep diving back into the options screen to change around the apps that have VPN access—though you can if you want. It means VPN peace of mind where you need it, without the inconvenience of having a VPN applied where it's not useful.

articles.title: Agribank giảm lãi suất cho vay tới 2,5% mỗi năm hỗ trợ sản xuất kinh doanh
articles.text:
Theo đó, Agribank giảm lãi suất cho vay tới 2,5 %/năm đối với dư nợ hiện hữu, tùy theo đối tượng và mức lãi suất đang áp dụng; đồng thời, quy định mức lãi suất cho vay tối đa trên cơ sở thời hạn vay và đối tượng vay vốn.
Với việc triển khai chính sách giảm lãi suất cho vay này, Agribank sẽ giảm khoảng 2.000 tỷ đồng thu nhập thông qua chủ động tiết giảm chi phí, cân đối các nguồn lực. Đây là định hướng được Agribank kiên trì thực hiện xuyên suốt từ đầu năm 2026, góp phần duy trì mặt bằng lãi suất cho vay hợp lý và tạo điều kiện thuận lợi để khách hàng tiếp cận vốn vay ngân hàng. Thông qua các đợt điều chỉnh giảm lãi suất và chương trình tín dụng ưu đãi, từ đầu năm đến nay, Agribank đã giảm gần 6.000 tỷ đồng thu nhập lãi.
Để chính sách được triển khai kịp thời, thực chất, đồng bộ, bảo đảm đầy đủ quyền lợi của khách hàng, Agribank quán triệt các đơn vị trong toàn hệ thống nghiêm túc thực hiện việc giảm lãi suất cho vay hoàn thành trước ngày 25/10/2026. Đồng thời, tăng cường kiểm tra, giám sát, kịp thời phát hiện, chấn chỉnh và kiên quyết xử lý các cá nhân, đơn vị không tuân thủ chỉ đạo về giảm lãi suất cho vay.
Đối với khách hàng doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa vay vốn phục vụ hoạt động sản xuất kinh doanh, Agribank dành 70.000 tỷ đồng triển khai chương tín dụng ưu đãi với lãi suất cho vay thấp hơn 1 - 2%/năm so với lãi suất cho vay bình quân cùng kỳ hạn.
Cùng với đó, Agribank tiếp tục triển khai nhiều chương trình tín dụng ưu đãi theo đối tượng khách hàng, lĩnh vực sản xuất, kinh doanh và các lĩnh vực ưu tiên của nền kinh tế với tổng quy mô hơn 500.000 tỷ đồng, lãi suất thấp hơn 2 - 2,5%/năm so với lãi suất cho vay thông thường.
Đây là hành động cụ thể, thể hiện quyết tâm và trách nhiệm của Agribank trong việc thực hiện hiệu quả chỉ đạo của Chính phủ, Ngân hàng Nhà nước, tiết giảm chi phí, giảm thu nhập để giảm lãi suất cho vay hỗ trợ khách hàng, hướng tín dụng vào các lĩnh vực ưu tiên, lĩnh vực sản xuất kinh doanh mang lại giá trị cho nền kinh tế, góp phần thúc đẩy tăng trưởng kinh tế bền vững.
Thông tin chi tiết về chính sách giảm lãi suất và các chương trình tín dụng ưu đãi, khách hàng liên hệ Chi nhánh, Phòng giao dịch của Agribank để được hỗ trợ, tư vấn.
(Nguồn: Agribank)

articles.title: Carta and NewView partner, hoping to entice more startups to let employees sell shares early | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Startups are staying private longer, leaving employees, who typically take a portion of their compensation as stock they can’t sell, with little hope of early liquidity.
An increasing number of late-stage startups are recognizing this and offering tender offers to employees. These are transactions that allow employees (and, often, early investors) to sell a portion of their shares for a predetermined price to an approved investor.
To simplify the tender process, NewView Capital recently partnered with Carta. The collaboration combines NewView’s secondary deal-structuring experience with Carta’s equity platform. Ravi Viswanathan, founder and managing partner of NewView, pitches this as a way to help startups launch and manage liquidity programs more seamlessly.
“The hope is that this partnership will make it easier for CEOs and companies to think about tenders,” he said. He wants founders to think about giving employees early liquidity as a “win-win-win” for workers, companies, and investors alike.
A growing number of startups seem to agree. Over the past three years, tender offers increased threefold for Series C and later-stage startups, according to a recent study from NewView and Carta. Plus, the startups that do choose tender offers are no longer just the most valuable private companies, like OpenAI, Databricks, or Anduril, according to Viswanathan.
For instance, last year, his firm, which specializes in secondary deals along with typical venture investments, helped facilitate a tender for Hightouch at a $1.3 billion valuation, when the marketing customization startup was seven years old.
However, Carta and NewView also found that the overall share of startups launching these offerings remains relatively small, with just 44 executed in the first half of 2026. So Viswanathan wants to encourage other startups to consider tender offers, calling them excellent retention tools and morale boosters.
A decade ago, being a unicorn was enough to attract talent, Viswanathan said, but with so many billion-dollar companies around today, that status may not be as much of a draw now. Offering a tender, he said, “is an opportunity to say you will also get liquidity in your journey with us.”
Some of the companies that recently held tender offers include AI customer support startup Decagon, self-driving tech developer Wayve, and AI voice generator ElevenLabs, which executed two such offerings in less than a year.
“The companies are staying private for 12 to 15 years. That’s not changing,” Viswanathan said. “In that interim, so that we don’t have this talent drain from high-quality venture-backed companies into their public counterparts, we need to make sure that there is liquidity for the employees.”

articles.title: Turtle Beach’s Vulcan II XP Is a Flashy Keyboard With a Flawed Finish
articles.text:
Highly customizable, both physically and through software tweaks. Great to type on. Reliably responsive inputs. Excellent macro manager.
TIRED
No Hall effect keys. Inverted media wheel and some non-functioning LEDs. Plastic basin underside feels cheap.
Turtle Beach is no stranger to competitive-grade gaming keyboards. In recent years, it has focused on its mid- to high-tier Vulcan range, with the Vulcan II XP as its newest entry.
It has a lot going for it—Titan HS mechanical switches, easy modification and customization options, and a suite of pro-tier gaming features available through its support software. However, while it arrives as a full-size keyboard (NumPad included!), a series of trade-offs and compromises ultimately make it feel very middle-of-the-pack.
Measuring 462 x 153 x 32 millimeters, it looks undeniably sharp thanks to its low profile and floating-key approach, all sitting atop a premium brushed-aluminum top plate. Unfortunately, the first compromise is the disappointing underside: a cheap-feeling basic plastic shell basin. Thankfully, the legs feel sturdy when popped up, adding around 10 mm in height and a comfortable angle to the board.
I also like the included soft foam wrist rest, which snaps to the front underside and adds nice support when gaming or typing. It's not memory foam, though, so I fear it might lose some of that cushion over time. The Vulcan also has integrated media controls on the top right with back, play/pause, and forward buttons, plus a media wheel with a push-to-mute feature.
It’s a $150 wired-only device (Turtle Beach is launching a wireless version, the Vulcan II XP Air for an extra $50) that connects via a detachable 1.8-meter USB-C to USB-A cord. A physical connection means zero input latency, which competitive gamers will benefit from.
Swarm Mode
The corded approach does make the Vulcan II XP a breeze to set up. Plug it into a Windows PC, and that's it. But you’ll need Turtle Beach’s Swarm II app to get the most out of it, especially given that the default RGB lighting is a blinding rainbow cascade.
Swarm II brings out the best in this keyboard. Visually, it offers 10 built-in customizable light effects—you can adjust brightness, pattern speed, and colors for some templates. They're pretty gimmicky—especially the Snake one—but it makes for a fun showcase. What's cooler is that you can adjust every LED, perfect for the 11th “custom” slot where you can choose colors, speed, and one of six patterns. You can turn the LEDs off entirely, but only through the app.
Beyond the eye candy, Turtle Beach packs in an impressive slate of features. You can remap inputs down to the individual key and store those configurations as one of five onboard profiles—perfect if you want layouts tailored to specific games, or a more work-oriented profile.
Critical to the keyboard’s gaming credentials, it includes a macro manager that lets you create custom inputs and command combos, down to how many milliseconds of input it should take before activating a keypress. It supports dozens of popular games by default, from competitive favorites like Counter-Strike and Overwatch to single-player epics like Skyrim, which have popular modding scenes and can benefit from bespoke controls. It even has presets for office apps and Photoshop, adding to the Vulcan’s overall versatility. You can easily import new layouts, too.
Touch Typing
I’ve been testing the version with linear switches—Turtle Beach also offers a model with tactile switches, both available in black or white. If you’re new to mechanical keyboards, the main difference is that linear keys press all the way down smoothly, while tactile ones have a little “bump” of resistance as the internal switch activates, which you can feel as the keystroke registers. It’s ultimately personal preference.
For the most part, this is a joy to type on, with precise spacing between keys, and the keys themselves having a satisfying “clackiness” when fully pressed. The only small issue is that the factory-lubed linear keys are so smooth and silent until you get that clack as they hit the base, that it’s easy to accidentally long-press a key. Until you’re used to that, it can catch you off-guard—not an issue when typing, where the worst is an errant stretch of letters whennnnnnnn pausing to think mid-sentence, but it tripped me up a couple of times in games until I was used to it.
Unfortunately, unlike Turtle Beach’s earlier Vulcan II TKL Pro, the keys here aren’t Hall effect, but they are hot-swappable—another trade-off, exchanging long-term reliability and accuracy for the ability to replace or upgrade keys easily. The board supports three-pin or five-pin mechanical switch keys and makes swapping them easy. The flat keycaps also pop off without trouble, which makes cleaning simple. Turtle Beach claims the switches last 50 million keystrokes, which should be plenty, but only a third of the TKL Pro's 150 million.
In gaming, the Vulcan II XP offers a 1,000-Hz polling rate for a 1-millisecond response time, which is competition-grade but falls short of the higher-end 8,000-Hz keyboards on the market. Hopping back to Swarm II, you can activate its more advanced features, like Easy-Shift, allowing for key duplication—basically putting commonly used features within easier reach—and ReacTap, assigning two commands to the same key, useful for games that require very swift inputs. (This might be banned in some competitive scenes under automation rules, though.)
These features can be a little fiddly to set up and map, but with a little experimentation, you can build layouts and input fields that work exactly as you want or need. I tailored a bunch of controls for Borderlands 3 and was dropping Psychos like never before. A minor annoyance, though: Reverting a specific input while trying to create a custom setup would sometimes revert the entire profile, which meant I had to redo everything.
Back to the Drawing Board
While the Vulcan II XP offers great performance for the price, I do have concerns about the overall build quality. On the unit I received, the media wheel was inverted by default—turning it counter-clockwise toward the minus symbol turned the volume up. This was even after I updated the board’s firmware through the Swarm II app, and I had to remap the inputs for it to work as intended. It’s good that the Vulcan II XP’s customization is specific and nuanced enough to remap even the dial direction, but I shouldn’t have had to.
I also found that the LEDs below the “0” and “.” keys on the NumPad don’t seem to work properly, glowing a stubborn, glaring white no matter what color or pattern is assigned. I even tried turning off every other key’s light and manually assigning colors to just those—to no avail.
It’s another reason the board feels middle-of-the-road. Like the shiny metallic top plate hiding the cheaper plastic base, the Vulcan II XP dazzles at a glance, but the closer you look, the more flaws and small annoyances are revealed.
For the price, some of those annoyances are forgivable. For anyone who hasn't upgraded to a mechanical keyboard, this is a decent entry without breaking the bank, delivering a lovely typing experience backed up by enough pro-tier gaming features to feel like a real upgrade—but more demanding or professional players will want to aim higher.
Matt Kamen is a freelance journalist specializing in media, video games, and technology coverage. Beyond WIRED, his work can be found in The Guardian, Empire, and elsewhere. ... Read More

articles.title: From Toast to Bessemer: Who founders will hear from at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Building a startup means making decisions before you have all the answers.
When should you scale? How do you know you really have product-market fit? What does it take to land enterprise customers? How do you build the right team? And when you finally get in front of an investor, how do you make sure your pitch earns another conversation?
On November 4 at SoWa Power Station in Boston, TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 will bring together founders, investors, and operators who have tackled those questions from different sides of the table.
Hosted by TechCrunch in partnership with Fidelity Private Shares, the full-day event goes beyond fundraising and AI to explore the realities of finding customers, building teams, sharpening a pitch, developing founder leadership, and scaling companies both inside and outside traditional startup hubs. Save 25% on your ticket today, and bring a colleague along for free with our limited BOGO deal.
Some of the speakers founders will hear from in Boston
Steve Fredette on building a company that keeps reinventing itself
Boston founders do not have to look far for an example of what can happen when a startup finds its market and continues evolving with its customers.
Steve Fredette, president, co-founder, and director of Toast, takes the Impact Stage for “Building a Company That Keeps Reinventing Itself.”
Toast’s story offers founders a compelling case study in identifying a customer problem, finding product-market fit, winning customers, and ultimately scaling a Boston startup into a public company.
But reaching scale does not mean the work is finished. Fredette’s conversation will look at what it takes to continue evolving a company as customer expectations, technology, and the market change around it, while staying connected to the needs that helped create the business in the first place.
Kent Bennett on knowing when product-market fit is real
Growth can be exciting. Growing too early can be expensive.
Kent Bennett, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, will lead “Finding Product Market Fit Before You Scale,” focusing on one of the most important questions an early-stage founder can answer: Are customers actually telling you that you are ready to grow?
The session will give founders a chance to think more critically about the signals that matter before adding headcount, increasing spend, or accelerating go-to-market efforts.
It is a useful counterpoint to startup culture’s constant pressure to move faster. Sometimes the smartest next move is making sure the foundation is actually there.
Rudina Seseri on when to scale and when to hit the brakes
That same tension takes center stage with Rudina Seseri, founder and managing partner of Glasswing Ventures.
In “When to Scale and When to Hit the Brakes,” Seseri will explore how founders can distinguish between the moments that call for acceleration and the moments when restraint may protect the business.
Founders are constantly making trade-offs between growth and discipline. Knowing when not to scale can be just as consequential as knowing when to go all in.
Lior Div on building for AI from day one
AI is reshaping how new companies think about products, operations, and teams, but adding AI to an existing process is different from building a company around it from the start.
Lior Div, CEO and co-founder of 7AI, will tackle that distinction in “Built for AI From Day One.”
For founders building in the current technology environment, the conversation provides an opportunity to think beyond AI as a feature and toward how it can influence the architecture and operating model of an entire company.
Chase Garbarino on the Boston founder playbook
The startup world does not begin and end in Silicon Valley.
Chase Garbarino, CEO and co-founder of HqO, will take the Impact Stage for “The Boston Founder Playbook,” examining what it means to build and scale a company from Boston.
For founders across New England and the broader East Coast ecosystem, the conversation offers a particularly relevant perspective on talent, customers, capital, and community outside the Bay Area.
Combined with Fredette’s Toast story, it also gives this year’s Summit a strong local through line: Ambitious companies can be built in Boston, and founders here do not need to copy Silicon Valley to do it.
Dave Balter on the pitch that gets you another meeting
A pitch does not have to close the deal. It has to make someone want the next conversation.
Dave Balter, venture partner at True Ventures and CEO of Edisyl, will explore that idea in “Your Pitch Has to Earn the Next Conversation.”
For founders accustomed to explaining their companies every day, the session is a reminder that knowing your business and communicating its story are two different skills.
Later in the afternoon, attendees will see that theory put into practice.
Catch the full list of Founders Summit speakers here.
Watch founders pitch live
At “So You Think You Can Pitch?,” founders will put their stories to the test live on the Build Stage.
Balter will be joined by Chirag Shah, partner at Define Ventures, and Simran Suri, principal at Maveron, as startups make their cases in front of an investor judging panel.
For attendees, it is an opportunity to watch what happens when founders have limited time to make an idea connect, and to hear how investors react in real time.
It is one of the most interactive parts of the Founder Summit program and a chance to learn from both the pitches that land and the ones that leave questions unanswered.
More than one startup conversation
The rest of the program stretches across many of the decisions founders are facing right now.
Hunter Worland of NEA will explore why distribution may become a startup’s next competitive advantage. Vineet Edupuganti, co-founder and CEO of Cogent Security, will discuss building 10x teams. Tina Tosukhowong of TDK Ventures will examine the hidden signals that can identify category winners.
Fidelity Private Shares will also bring its perspective to conversations about fundraising trends with Kristen Craft and enterprise relationships with Evan Schnidman.
Together, the agenda creates a day that is not just about raising the next round or chasing the latest AI trend but is also about building the company.
Join the conversation in Boston
TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 takes place November 4 at SoWa Power Station in Boston.
The day brings together candid founder conversations, practical sessions, smaller roundtables, live pitching, networking, and a closing reception presented by Fidelity Private Shares.
With the event approaching quickly and only so many spots left, don’t wait to register! Act now on our limited time offer and save 25% on your Founder Summit ticket.

articles.title: These Headphones Twist Into a Bluetooth Speaker in Seconds. If Only They Sounded Better
articles.text:
Unveiled at CES 2026, the TDM Neo is a pair of on-ear headphones that transform into a Bluetooth speaker. It caught the imagination of the attending media, won a handful of awards, and inspired countless column inches.
Given the current state of the portable audio industry, it's easy to understand why. Most designs seem to revolve around incremental updates and new colorways rather than genuine technical innovation. Neo is an exciting alternative, and it’s little wonder the startup brand went on to smash its Kickstarter targets.
I’ve spent the past couple of weeks listening to the headphones and Bluetooth speaker, and have lost count of the number of times I’ve showed off the clever twist-and-fold mechanism to friends. But has TDM managed to produce a genuine tech twofer, or designed a novelty product that gives you the worst of both worlds?
Twist and Shout
The twist-and-fold mechanism on the Neo is clever and addictive. Rotate the ear cups around the cushioned but flexible headband, bring them together, and strong magnets snap everything firmly in place. Once connected, the headphone drivers disable, and the outward-facing Bluetooth speakers kick in. Twist them apart and you've got your headphones back.
It’s innovative, and the engineering is impressive. Once in speaker mode, the two rubber TDM logos sit closely together and form a protective base, while the asymmetrical twisted headband cocoons the ear cups together. It works well—it never once popped open accidentally. The action is smooth, the connection reassuringly solid, and switching between modes works exactly as intended.
The Neo has four 40-mm drivers—two for the headphones and two for the speakers. The outward-facing speakers are each rated at 5 watts (for a total of 10). Ten watts is not a lot for a modern Bluetooth speaker, but wattage doesn't automatically tell you how loud or good a speaker will sound, especially in the current age of digital signal processing. The highly regarded $55 JBL Go 5 has just 4.5 watts of output, for instance.

Theo biểu lãi suất huy động dành cho khách hàng cá nhân có hiệu lực từ ngày 23/10 của PGBank, lãi suất ngân hàng giảm 0,5 điểm phần trăm đối với kỳ hạn 6-13 tháng của sản phẩm tiền gửi tiết kiệm thông thường và lãi suất tiền gửi “Phúc An Khang”.
Theo đó, lãi suất tiết kiệm kỳ hạn 1-5 tháng của hai sản phẩm tiền gửi này vẫn giữ nguyên 4,75%/năm, trong khi lãi suất tiết kiệm 6-9 tháng giảm còn 6,1%/năm, kỳ hạn 12-13 tháng giảm còn 6,2%/năm, kỳ hạn 18-36 tháng được giữ nguyên ở mức 6,8%/năm.
Tuy nhiên, PGBank giữ nguyên lãi suất tiền gửi trực tuyến với biểu lãi suất hiện tại, gồm: Kỳ hạn 1-5 tháng là 4,75%/năm, kỳ hạn 6-9 tháng là 6,9%/năm, kỳ hạn 12-13 tháng là 7%/năm, kỳ hạn 18-36 tháng là 6,8%/năm.
Ngoài biểu lãi suất ngân hàng công bố, trong một số trường hợp đặc biệt, PGBank có thể áp dụng mức lãi suất khác với biểu niêm yết.
Cũng trong sáng nay, Ngân hàng TMCP Sài Gòn Công Thương (Saigonbank) giảm lãi suất tiền gửi các kỳ hạn từ 6-12 tháng và 18-36 tháng với mức giảm 0,5 điểm phần trăm.

articles.title: Agent cloud startup Daytona hits $1B valuation backed by FirstMark and a who’s who of angels | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Daytona Platforms announced on Friday that it had raised a $60 million Series B round at a $1 billion valuation led by FirstMark Growth. The company says it has now raised a total of $91 million.
The New York-based startup has attracted not just FirstMark (which also led its $24 million Series A in February), but also a host of well-known angels in this latest round. Daytona says they include Stripe’s Patrick Collison, Shopify’s Tobi Lütke, Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas, Zoom’s Eric Yuan, Datadog’s Olivier Pomel, Quora’s Adam D’Angelo (who is also an OpenAI board member), and Mercor’s Brendan Foody. It also names Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next, and Okta Ventures as participants.
Three-year-old Daytona is building a cloud specifically for long-running agents, which have different infrastructure needs than yesteryear’s software, the startup contends. “Agents don’t work like the long-lived services today’s cloud was designed for. They spin up thousands of short, stateful jobs nobody planned in advance, and they need a cloud built for that,” founder Ivan Burazin wrote in a blog post announcing the new round. Daytona’s cloud, he said, is like giving every agent its own computer, where agents have access to sandboxed versions of Linux, Windows, macOS, and GPUs, among other services, on the one platform.

articles.title: A Dating App Is Offering ‘Chivalry Mode’ and ‘Marriage Timeline’ to Get Gen Z Married
articles.text:
When Adreanna Pulliam signed up for the Christian dating app Upward over the summer, she was prepared to come across men who identified as hyperconservative.
So when she swiped on a guy’s profile that listed “a progressive donkey or a ‘Trump is King’ elephant” as his relationship deal-breaker, she was shocked. “I hadn’t expected to see a moderate libertarian” on the app, she says.
It only got more bizarre from there. There was the guy advertising his Snapchat with the username “Yaboi Blaze reallysexgod.” Another dater, for reasons she still can’t fathom, included a photo of him at a funeral, standing in front of a poster-size image of the deceased.
While Pulliam was apprehensive about the prospects, she wanted to see how different Upward, one of the lesser-known apps in Match Group’s sprawling portfolio of dating platforms, was from Hinge and Tinder. She hadn’t had much luck with either of them. Many of the profiles she encountered on Upward, she tells WIRED, were “MAGA types of men” who “fit more of that red-pill, trad wife, conservative values” category of dater.
A 25-year-old opera singer in Bloomington, Indiana, for whom marriage has always been “the end goal,” Pulliam is the kind of person Upward is trying to appeal to since relaunching last month.
The relaunch was redesigned around two key data points from Match Group’s 2026 Singles in America study: 72 percent of Gen Zs want to get married, and a quarter of singles aged 18 to 34 “identify with a combination of traditional values around family, faith, and community,” a news release about the survey noted.
The pivot away from an app exclusively for Christian daters was about opening up its doors for people “who share those same goals, but may not lead with a faith-first mindset,” says Lauren DeFord, director of brand marketing at Match, of the app’s new focus on Gen Z singles.
Upward’s expansion is representative of the ongoing change in the dating market. Dwindling engagement and the introduction of AI have pushed companies to reassess user growth. For some, that means abandoning their original mission.
Upward, which runs on a tiered subscription, works similarly to Tinder. You can swipe left or right on profiles, and users are encouraged to include a Faith Statement on their page, explaining what they value most about their relationship to God. Among its new features are Chivalry Mode, which, if you’re familiar with how Bumble used to operate, persuades men to message first, and Marriage Timeline, which lets daters share when they hope to get married with potential suitors.
But while a marriage-focused app like Upward may be tapping into a genuine desire for commitment, that doesn’t mean young people are returning to traditional relationship norms en masse, says Daniel Cox, author of Generation Uncoupled: America’s New Gender Divide and the Crisis of Human Connection. In fact, the opposite is happening.
In his book, Cox argues that Gen Z is entering adulthood with a less clear sense of their “relational priorities,” and a decline in social and civic life has given rise to a “hyperindividualistic culture” that doesn’t always prioritize things like marriage. As a result, fewer Gen Zs are coupling up today. An American Institute for Boys and Men survey found that 44 percent of Gen Z men have had no relationship experience at all during their teen years, double the rate for older men. “This movement makes it a lot harder to ... want to sacrifice and to be there for someone,” he says.
Upward’s relaunch framed the app as the “home of modern courtship,” including video testimonials of singles who’d found love on the app. But aesthetically, there wasn’t anything “modern” about its promotional rollout. In one video, newly married Zach donned a cowboy hat and blue jeans, doing all the things men should presumably do for their significant others: gift them flowers, carry her through a meadow, open the car door. A bold text overlay on the video read “chivalrymaxxing.” According to the company, branding was inspired by an “Americana” theme, and its “Wanted: For Life” campaign draws on Western-style imagery.
Cox, who is the director of the Survey Center on American Life, is convinced that the trad trend is “a reaction to the lack of cultural norms around courtship. People are wanting something over nothing,” he says, adding that daters are desperate for “a script” with direction and defined roles, given how nontraditional approaches to partnership, such as polyamory and relationship anarchy, are increasing among young people. “And something that’s nice about the trad script is it’s very clear. Though I don’t think it’s close to ideal for a lot of young people.”
A 2023 Pew Research survey found that only 23 percent of adults considered being married “extremely” or “very important” to living a fulfilling life, compared with 61 percent who said the same about having close friends. In the last 30 years, the percentage of high school seniors who said they were likely to marry someday had fallen from 80 percent in 1993 to 67 percent in 2023, according to Pew. The decline was driven mostly by changing views among young women who, despite the portion of married adults slightly increasing from 50 percent to 51 percent between 2019 to 2023, remain more likely than men to be unpartnered.
The trend is likely to continue in that direction. “There’s increasingly a belief among young women that marriage makes them less happy,” Cox says. “So it’s not only that they have less of a desire to get married. There’s a concern that if they get married, they won’t be as happy as if they are single. That seems like a view that is potentially not going to change.”
Upward, which declined to share information regarding the number of active users on the platform, is betting that it will.
When setting up her account, Pulliam was baffled to find out that Upward let users list their body type, ranging from “fit” and “curvy” to “chubby,” a feature typically reserved for hookup apps. She was also confused that Upward allows married people on the app. Some of the stranger options for relationship type included “it’s complicated” and “I’m not into labels.” “I’m not knocking open relationships or anything like that, but it was interesting to see such a progressive take from a more of a conservative demographic,” she says.
Tauti, a social work student who lives in California, lasted less than 48 hours on the app, disturbed by the overwhelming conservative majority looking for domesticated partners. Sometimes the hook with mission-specific apps like Upward is that the religious identity associated with the platform can create an assumption of compatibility before users have really gotten to know one another. “I did not know me being Christian and leaning liberal was a big ask,” she said on TikTok. “It’s turned me off from Christian dating altogether.”
Some users believe the recent pivot is diluting the experience for daters who joined seeking out people with purely Christian beliefs. “Why are you on there if you’re agnostic?” Heidi Marais, a teacher and single mom, asked on TikTok in September. “And Upward, why is it an option?”
DeFord, who maintains that Christian singles remain at the core of Upward’s mission despite describing the relaunch as a “brand shift,” pushes back against the assertion that the experience is worsening. “Those users can still interact and match with people who share the same denomination, the same religious views, the same cadence of how they like to practice.”
Since its debut in 2020, Upward has struggled with various hiccups that include everything from functionality issues to user perception. Many reviews in the Apple App Store complain of terrible user support, poor filtering features, and automatic bans, with one user calling the app “janky as hell.”
Cox notes there is ample reason to be wary of Match’s claim that a majority of Gen Z want to get married. Given that Gen Z is younger, it is likely that more people have never tied the knot. “So if they’re comparing Gen Z to millennials or Gen Xers in the survey, it could be that they have already been in relationships, maybe even divorced, so they are not as eager to get married again.” Match’s survey, which the company says is “demographically representative” of the US Census, sampled 5,000 US singles over the age of 18 who were not married, living with a partner, or in a committed relationship. In any case, Cox says, the “norm around what is the ideal age to get married” has vanished.
Pulliam still wants to get hitched but doesn’t consider it a priority right now. She attended a Christian college and recognizes the potential for Upward to be a hit “within communities of Christian private universities,” she says. “But I think the only way that the app works is for maybe someone who has a little bit more of a closed mind.”

articles.title: Giá bạc rơi thẳng đứng, bạc thỏi 'bốc hơi' gần 2 triệu đồng/kg sau 1 đêm
articles.text:
Giá bạc trong nước đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay đồng loạt được các thương hiệu điều chỉnh giảm sâu.
Mở cửa phiên giao dịch hôm nay, giá bạc của Công ty TNHH MTV Vàng bạc Đá quý Ngân hàng Sài Gòn Thương Tín (Sacombank - SBJ) được điều chỉnh giảm rất mạnh.
Lúc 9h08', giá bạc miếng của SBJ được điều chỉnh xuống mức 1,86-1,92 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán), còn giá bạc thỏi về ngưỡng 49,6-51,2 triệu đồng/kg (mua - bán). So với kết phiên giao dịch hôm qua, giá bạc miếng của SBJ giảm 72.000 đồng/lượng, trong khi giá bạc thỏi của thương hiệu này hạ tới 1,92 triệu đồng/kg ở cả chiều mua và bán.
Tương tự, giá bạc tại Tập đoàn Vàng bạc Đá quý Phú Quý sáng nay cũng giảm mạnh.
Đầu phiên hôm nay, giá bạc miếng tại Tập đoàn Vàng bạc Đá quý Phú Quý được điều chỉnh giảm 53.000 đồng/lượng ở chiều mua và rẻ hơn 54.000 đồng/lượng ở chiều bán so với chốt phiên hôm qua, xuống mức 1,86-1,918 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán).
Giá bạc thỏi của thương hiệu này vào đầu phiên hạ xuống mức 49,599-51,146 triệu đồng/kg (mua - bán), giảm tới 1,414 triệu đồng/kg ở chiều mua và rẻ hơn 1,44 triệu đồng/kg ở chiều bán so với kết phiên hôm qua.
Cùng xu hướng, giá bạc miếng của Công ty CP Kim loại quý Ancarat đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay cũng hạ nhanh.
Lúc 9h05', giá bạc miếng Ancarat được niêm yết ở mức 1,844-1,901 triệu đồng/lượng (mua - bán), hạ 55.000 đồng/lượng ở chiều mua và rẻ hơn 57.000 đồng/lượng ở chiều bán so với mức chốt hôm qua.
Cùng thời điểm, giá bạc thỏi của Ancarat được giao dịch ở mức 49,173-50,693 triệu đồng/kg (mua - bán), giảm 1,467 triệu đồng/kg ở chiều mua và rẻ hơn 1,52 triệu đồng/kg ở chiều bán so với kết phiên hôm qua.
Giá bạc trên thị trường quốc tế cũng có xu hướng đi xuống. Lúc 9h49' ngày 23/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá bạc giao ngay được niêm yết ở mức 53,96 USD/ounce, giảm 0,93% so với phiên trước.
Giá bạc thế giới suy giảm khi kỳ vọng về việc Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed) thắt chặt chính sách tiền tệ và lo ngại nhu cầu công nghiệp suy yếu gây sức ép lên giá.
Trong tháng 9, chỉ số giá tiêu dùng (CPI) của Mỹ tăng 0,6% so với tháng trước và 3,7% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái. Áp lực giá kéo dài có thể khiến Fed thận trọng hơn với việc nới lỏng chính sách, thậm chí làm gia tăng kỳ vọng tăng lãi suất vào cuối năm.
Trong khi đó, mặt bằng lãi suất cao thường gây bất lợi cho bạc do kim loại này không mang lại lợi suất. Dù thị trường nghiêng về khả năng Fed giữ nguyên lãi suất trong cuộc họp vào ngày 27-28/10 nhưng triển vọng tăng lãi suất vào tháng 12 vẫn là yếu tố khiến nhà đầu tư thận trọng.
Bên cạnh chính sách tiền tệ, giá bạc còn chịu tác động từ triển vọng sản xuất công nghiệp. Nếu hoạt động kinh tế suy yếu thì nhu cầu bạc trong các ngành công nghiệp sẽ giảm, điều này có thể gia tăng sức ép lên giá.

articles.title: Commonwealth Fusion Systems gets $85M to build better fusion-ready semiconductors | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) announced on Thursday that it would receive $85 million from the U.S. government to develop advanced chips for the fusion power industry.
Fusion power startups have been racing to complete their first demonstration devices, with CFS aiming to turn on its Sparc reactor sometime next year. But building one reactor is just a proof point. If fusion startups want to build dozens of commercial power plants, they’ll need more durable power electronics and a robust supply chain.
The new CHIPS Act award from the Department of Commerce, which also grants the government a stake in CFS, will help boost R&D and manufacturing capacity for semiconductors in the U.S., the company said.
“Ultimately, that means a more capable, economical power plant and a stronger U.S. supply chain to build it,” Brandon Sorbom, co-founder and chief science officer at CFS, wrote in a blog post.
CFS’s award will go toward supporting five different initiatives.
The first is the advancement of silicon carbide power electronics. The semiconductors are widely used to manage high voltages, and they’re found in everything from LEDs and EVs to cell phone base stations and data centers. It’s also used in fusion machines, where intense bursts of electricity are used to drive the superconducting magnets that confine plasma inside a reactor.
CFS will also use the award to develop next-generation radio-frequency power generators, which the company uses to heat fusion fuel, and advanced electronics that will enable faster control of the reactor and be hardened against radiation. The latter could help extend the lifespan of electronics within a fusion power plant, reducing operating costs.
Lastly, CFS plans to use part of the CHIPS award to adapt AI hardware like GPUs and TPUs for power plants.
“The funding would help improve the U.S. chip and power electronics industries at the same time it accelerates fusion energy’s progress toward the electrical grid,” Sorbom said.

articles.title: These Smart Bird Feeders Make Great Gifts. They’re Already on Sale
articles.text:
You know who doesn’t care about AI, recession indicators, or You Can See Everything FOMO? Birds.
Birds don’t even know you exist, nor would they care about you if they did. In this era of everything all the time, it’s almost life-affirming to interact with a being who has a brain the size of a garbanzo bean, that isn't able to drive or vote.
There are probably entertaining dramas playing out in your yard right now that you don’t even know about. Mine include a crow with one eye and a greedy Steller’s jay that fills his crop with peanuts until it’s translucent.
Now that smart bird feeders have been around since 2020, even moderately priced models come with high-resolution cameras, 4K video recording, and AI ID that rarely misses. Many of them require minimal maintenance other than filling the seeds. (As long as you're following the 5-7-9 rule of pole-mount placement, to keep squirrels away.)
Below are some early Black Friday sales on models I have been using and enjoying for years and would not hesitate to buy for a gift (or myself).
Top Picks
Birdfy Original (Blue) With Solar for $127 (29% Off)
For some reason, this deal is only on the blue version of this feeder; the yellow costs an extra ($13). Anyhow, if you've only got $130 to spend, Birdfy's enduring original is your best bet. Sure, there are sturdier, better-designed feeders (like Kiwibit, below), and feeders with better camera quality (like Camojojo's 32MP Hibird), but you will either pay extra or run into janky apps and paywalled features.
If you're just looking for a reliable feeder that will last through the seasons and sports a high-quality, easy-to-use app without major features being paywalled, you won't do better than this model. It comes with an auxiliary solar panel that mounts separately, but if you don't want solar, you can pay even less—just $110. I would recommend it, though—Birdfy's panels have been very reliable in my experience, and I think it's worth the extra $17 to not have to worry about bringing it in to charge. (Note: This model only supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.)
Kiwibit Feeder 2 With Solar Roof for $170 (29% Off)
This isn't the latest and greatest Kiwibit model (that would be the Feeder 2 Pro, $220), but the regular Feeder 2 is still exceedingly well designed, and this is the lowest price I have ever seen it. The generously sized, 1.5-liter seed hopper is bifurcated for two different types of feed and pulls right out of the body via a handle on the top—no need to take the whole feeder down to refill.
The 8-megapixel photos and 4K video quality are top-tier at this price point, and the solar roof kept everything charged through all kinds of weather during my test. The app is easy to navigate and functional without a Kiwibit Plus subscription, but more and more features are starting to be paywalled, as I found when I recently reviewed the Feeder 2 Pro, which I don't love. Note that this feeder only works on 2.4-GHz Wi-Fi and the warranty is only one year, compared with the above Birdfy's two-year warranty.
Kiwibit 4K Feeder With Auxiliary Solar for $140 (26% Off)
Despite the different name, this Kiwibit model has the same camera and hardware as the Feeder 2, just without the built-in solar roof. Still, I had no issues installing the included 3-watt solar panel on the back of the wall mount (I always pole-mount my feeders to keep squirrels away), so if you're interested in Kiwibit's sturdy build quality and high-resolution imagery and want to save $30, this is a totally viable option.

articles.title: What some of Anthropic’s backers are worth before its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Anthropic’s public listing, which is expected this year at a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, is bound to be a windfall for both early-stage and later-stage investors. But even at the company’s latest private market valuation of $965 billion, the stakes held by many of those VCs and early backers already total billions.
Coatue, which first backed Anthropic in 2025 at a $183 billion valuation and co-led the AI lab’s last two funding rounds, has poured a total of $4.75 billion into the company. That stake, based on the last round’s price, is now worth roughly $7.5 billion, according to a person familiar with the matter. Coatue declined to comment.
Below is what some other backers of Anthropic are worth based on the last round’s price, according to Bloomberg:
Eric Schmidt: The former Google CEO invested in Anthropic’s Series A in 2021, when the startup was valued at $461 million, according to PitchBook data. Today, Schmidt owns about 1% of the company, and even at its current private valuation, his stake is worth nearly $10 billion.
Iconiq: The investment outfit wrote a $6 billion check to Anthropic last year when the company was already valued at $183 billion. That massive late-stage bet is now worth $17 billion and has the potential to double at the IPO.
Menlo Ventures: The VC firm led Anthropic’s Series D and has invested more than $1 billion in the company over time, a stake now worth $14 billion.
Sequoia: The famed VC firm backed the AI lab for the first time only earlier this year, when the company was already valued at $380 billion. The $3 billion investment gave it about 1% ownership, which means it has already more than doubled its investment.
Sound Ventures: The firm, launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, invested $35 million in Anthropic’s 2023 Series C round and has since funneled an additional $400 million into the company, resulting in a stake that’s worth billions now. (Kutcher left Sound Ventures this year to launch a new VC firm.)
Spark Capital: The only VC firm known to hold a board seat at Anthropic invested $75 million in that same 2023 Series C round, when it was valued at $5 billion. That position has ballooned more than ninetyfold to $7 billion.
Updated to include Coatue’s returns.

articles.title: Tăng trưởng GDP hai con số: Tăng tốc đầu tư, đánh thức sức mua
articles.text:
Chính phủ đặt mục tiêu tăng trưởng GDP ít nhất 10% trong năm 2026, trong bối cảnh kinh tế đạt mức tăng trưởng 9,01% trong 9 tháng đầu năm. Tuy nhiên, theo doanh nghiệp và các chuyên gia, để duy trì đà tăng trưởng trong những tháng cuối năm, nền kinh tế cần những giải pháp cụ thể, tập trung vào khả năng tăng sản lượng, tạo thêm đơn hàng và nâng cao hiệu quả sử dụng nguồn lực.
Nhìn tăng trưởng ngay từ doanh nghiệp
Sức mua chậm trong ba quý đầu năm tạo áp lực lên doanh nghiệp, đặc biệt là khối sản xuất khi bước vào giai đoạn cuối năm. Với Vissan, thay vì chờ thị trường phục hồi, doanh nghiệp chủ động rà soát chi phí, làm việc với nhà cung cấp để hạn chế tăng giá đầu vào và dành thêm nguồn lực cho các chương trình khuyến mại.
Ông Phan Văn Dũng, Phó Tổng giám đốc Vissan, cho biết doanh nghiệp chấp nhận giảm lợi nhuận để đầu tư cho thị trường và kích cầu tiêu dùng. Phần chi phí tiết kiệm được sẽ dành cho các chương trình giảm giá 30-50%, nhằm thu hút người mua và tăng sản lượng tiêu thụ.
Theo ông Dũng, tăng trưởng kinh tế cần được nhìn từ sự phát triển của từng thành tố trong nền kinh tế. Với doanh nghiệp, việc giữ sức mua không chỉ phụ thuộc vào chính sách vĩ mô mà còn bắt đầu từ khả năng chủ động tiết giảm chi phí, điều chỉnh hoạt động và chia sẻ một phần khó khăn với người tiêu dùng.
Tuy nhiên, để những nỗ lực này phát huy hiệu quả, theo các chuyên gia cần thêm trợ lực từ phía nhà nước.
TS Huỳnh Thanh Điền, giảng viên Trường Đại học Nguyễn Tất Thành (TPHCM), cho rằng mục tiêu tăng trưởng hai con số cần được nhìn trong dài hạn, thay vì chỉ tập trung vào kết quả của riêng năm nay. Theo ông, trong những tháng cuối năm, cần phát huy vai trò của chính sách tài khóa, trước hết là đẩy nhanh đầu tư công và tháo gỡ vướng mắc pháp lý cho các dự án tư nhân.
Nhiều doanh nghiệp có sẵn nguồn vốn nhưng dự án vẫn đình trệ do thủ tục kéo dài. Nếu các vướng mắc được giải quyết kịp thời, doanh nghiệp có thể triển khai đầu tư, tạo việc làm và đưa dòng tiền vào nền kinh tế.
Ông cũng đề xuất tận dụng nhu cầu mua sắm cuối năm để kích cầu thông qua các chương trình bán hàng bình ổn giá, giảm giá và tổ chức lễ hội, du lịch. Khi người lao động có việc làm, thu nhập và chi tiêu, dòng tiền sẽ tiếp tục luân chuyển, thúc đẩy hoạt động kinh tế.
"Tôi vẫn tin rằng chúng ta sẽ đạt được tăng trưởng như kỳ vọng trong năm 2026 nếu quyết tâm tháo gỡ các khó khăn trên", TS Điền bày tỏ.
Cùng bàn về mục tiêu tăng trưởng hai con số, chuyên gia kinh tế TS Lê Bá Chí Nhân cho rằng cần chuyển từ tư duy điều hành theo chỉ tiêu sang quản trị tăng trưởng dựa trên năng suất, hiệu quả đầu tư và khả năng huy động nguồn lực.
Theo ông Nhân, đầu tư công cần đóng vai trò vốn mồi, trong khi đầu tư tư nhân mở rộng năng lực sản xuất. Xuất khẩu tạo nguồn thu ngoại tệ, còn tiêu dùng nội địa duy trì sức cầu và ổn định thị trường. TS Lê Bá Chí Nhân cũng nhấn mạnh, chính sách tài khóa và tiền tệ cần phối hợp chặt chẽ để vừa bảo đảm nguồn lực cho nền kinh tế, vừa kiểm soát lạm phát, ổn định tỷ giá và hạn chế rủi ro tài chính.
Từ góc nhìn thực tiễn, Thạc sĩ Nguyễn Tuấn Anh, chương trình Chính sách công Fulbright, phân tích, để duy trì đà tăng trưởng, cần xác định cụ thể những lĩnh vực còn khả năng tăng sản lượng trong các tháng cuối năm, doanh nghiệp nào có thể nhận thêm đơn hàng, công trình nào có thể hoàn thành ngay trong quý IV.
Theo ông, việc này cần bắt đầu từ những vướng mắc mà doanh nghiệp gặp hằng ngày. Khi thủ tục được giải quyết kịp thời, doanh nghiệp có thể sản xuất, giao hàng sớm hơn và tận dụng tốt cơ hội thị trường.
Đối với đầu tư công, cần ưu tiên những dự án đã sẵn sàng triển khai, có thể hoàn thành và đưa vào sử dụng. Việc giải ngân không chỉ cần nhanh mà còn phải gắn với tiến độ, chất lượng và hiệu quả thực tế của công trình.
“Riêng TPHCM, mức tăng GRDP 9 tháng đạt 9,06% là một nền tảng tích cực. Luật Phát triển đô thị cùng các nghị quyết của HĐND có hiệu lực từ ngày 1/10/2026 mở thêm điều kiện để thành phố triển khai các cơ chế mới. Để tăng trưởng cuối năm, cần rà soát và chọn ra những dự án, cơ sở sản xuất, hoạt động dịch vụ có thể tạo thêm giá trị ngay trong quý IV", ông Tuấn Anh đề xuất.
Tăng tốc nhưng không đánh đổi ổn định vĩ mô
Theo các chuyên gia, áp lực hoàn thành mục tiêu tăng trưởng không đồng nghĩa với việc nới lỏng các nguyên tắc quản lý rủi ro. Nguồn lực cần được đưa vào những hoạt động có khả năng tạo ra giá trị thực, thay vì mở rộng đầu tư bằng mọi giá.
TS Lê Bá Chí Nhân cho rằng chính sách tiền tệ phải linh hoạt, bảo đảm thanh khoản nhưng không đồng nghĩa với nới lỏng tín dụng trên diện rộng. Dòng vốn cần hướng đến những hoạt động sản xuất, kinh doanh có hiệu quả thực chất. Việc điều hành tỷ giá cũng cần tính đến cung cầu thị trường, diễn biến đồng USD và cán cân thanh toán, tránh biến động quá mức gây khó khăn cho doanh nghiệp.
Cùng với đó, cần theo dõi sát giá năng lượng, lương thực và các mặt hàng thiết yếu để kiểm soát áp lực lạm phát. Theo ông Nhân, Việt Nam cần chuyển từ mô hình tăng trưởng dựa nhiều vào lượng vốn sang chú trọng năng suất và hiệu quả, qua đó tạo nền tảng cho tăng trưởng bền vững.
Đồng quan điểm, ThS Nguyễn Tuấn Anh cho rằng không nên tăng vay vốn hoặc cấp vốn cho những dự án hiệu quả thấp chỉ để cải thiện kết quả tăng trưởng trong ngắn hạn.
Thay vào đó, cần sử dụng hiệu quả nguồn lực ngân sách đã bố trí và giải quyết các thủ tục đang cản trở dòng tiền của doanh nghiệp. Việc hoàn thuế đúng hạn, thanh toán khối lượng công trình đã nghiệm thu theo quy định và tháo gỡ vướng mắc hành chính sẽ giúp doanh nghiệp có thêm nguồn lực mua nguyên liệu, trả lương và duy trì sản xuất.
Đối với tín dụng, cần căn cứ vào nhu cầu thực tế và khả năng trả nợ, không hạ chuẩn cho vay để chạy theo mục tiêu tăng trưởng. Chính sách hỗ trợ cũng nên tập trung vào những nhóm chịu tác động lớn, tránh trợ giá dàn trải, kéo dài gây áp lực lên ngân sách.
Theo ông Tuấn Anh, kết quả tăng trưởng cuối năm không nên chỉ được đánh giá qua một chỉ tiêu GDP, mà còn cần nhìn vào sức khỏe doanh nghiệp, việc làm và thu nhập của người dân. Điều quan trọng là tạo được nền tảng sản xuất tốt hơn để bước sang năm 2027, thay vì để lại những khoản nợ và công trình kém hiệu quả.

articles.title: Hindsight pitches a $1M guarantee as Perspective API ends
articles.text:
Starting January 1, any moderation pipeline calling Perspective will fail. Google’s Jigsaw unit shuts the service down on December 31, ending one of the most widely used tools for scoring online comments for toxicity. For platforms, publishers, marketplaces, and communities built on it, the next few months bring an unwelcome decision. Find a replacement, and fast.
Hindsight wants to be that replacement. But rather than pitching a standard vendor swap, it is offering something no AI content moderation vendor has offered before, a professional guarantee against harm caused by content its model misses.
“Coded Language is the new slur, but it’s ridiculously hard to catch consistently,” said Dean Gebert, Hindsight’s Founder. “And a like-for-like model or tool swap just moves Perspective’s blind spots to a different vendor.”
Forced Migration Doubles as an Enterprise Audit
Most companies will treat Perspective’s shutdown as a routine engineering ticket. Hindsight sees it as a chance to ask a harder question: was the old tool delivering accurate protection in the first place?
Perspective scores how toxic a comment “sounds” on the surface. That works well on obvious insults. It works poorly on language designed to look harmless.
Bad actors know this, which is why they’ve shifted to Coded Language: numeric codes like “1488,” extremist slang like “boogaloo,” swapped characters (called “l33tspe@k”), and misspellings that mimic a slur’s phonetic sound like “phag“. The cost and liability show up in forums, posts, comments, bios, DMs, printed material, and more.
And it isn’t limited to English. Even a US-only platform has posts in Spanish and dozens of other languages, so Coded Language travels with them. Hindsight was pre-trained on 110 languages, meaning it can follow Coded Language across all of them without a separate model for each language.
The stakes are real. From 2016 to mid-2022, the Anti-Defamation League found that extremists raised at least $6.2 million across 324 crowdfunding campaigns. Also, more than 30 federal cases against a major gaming platform allege that its safeguards failed young users. And finally, merchandise with white nationalist messaging still appears on major online marketplaces.
Behind each of these was a moderation system that was supposed to be working. Perspective’s shutdown creates the opportunity for a rethink.
Why Binary Models Are Forced into a Compromise
Many moderation tools rely on rigid binary logic: Safe or Unsafe. That creates a lose-lose trade-off for platform executives. Tune the system to be strict, and it floods human reviewers with false alarms on everyday slang. Tune it to be lenient, and it misses the content that creates liability.
Hindsight’s 3 classes, Red Flag, Yellow Flag, and Safe, create a middle lane for ambiguous, context-dependent language. Automation clears the easy cases, allowing human reviewers to spend time on the harder edge cases (which go back into fine-tuning that client’s instance).
Gebert acknowledges these conversations can be uncomfortable, so his “safest example” is the word bitch, which can be derogatory or adoring depending on context. Aimed at a person in anger (who the hell is this bitch?), it’s a clear Red Flag. Between friends (she’s the baddest bitch I know), it’s likely Safe. But a binary model still can’t tell these apart.
“Consistently sorting contextual text into an accurate Yellow Flag category was extremely painful,” Gebert laughs. “It took equal doses of obsession, stubbornness, and lattes. But it’ll let clients rely less on human oversight and get more accurate results, so it’ll pay off.”
What the Benchmarks Show
Hindsight benchmarked 9 AI content moderation models (Mistral, OpenAI, Meta, Azure, AWS, and others) against a fixed set of 2,205 real online posts. A human labeled each as Red Flag, Yellow Flag, or Safe, and Hindsight’s model variants never saw any of the posts during development or training.
On Coded Language, Hindsight detected 97.9% of cases. Other models scored 65% and below. Its Missed Flag rate was 3.3% and its False Alarm rate was 8.2%. The company publishes the full benchmark methodology and results on its website, with the ability for companies to test Hindsight with their data.
The Efficiency of Specialization: Sniper vs. Shotgun
The result is a direct challenge to the assumption that larger models always perform better. Hindsight does not use 1 large, general-purpose base model. It builds on 3 specialized base models, each with fewer than 600 million parameters, and the company says the result outperforms models up to 14 times its size. Gebert calls it more sniper, less shotgun.
Its training data is intentionally narrow, with 83 MB of real online posts, drawn from 18 datasets (roughly 37 Harry Potter books), including 292,000 posts labeled by human reviewers. Across 164 trained variants, the company tracked how each performed and promoted the best variant to Champion.
What a $1M Guarantee Changes
Enterprise AI content moderation is typically sold as a cost center. It reduces risk, but few vendors guarantee an outcome. Hindsight changes that. If its model labels a post as Safe and that post causes a documented liability event, the client has up to $1 million in financial support, instead of an apology and a patch.
For teams facing the deadline, the practical pitch is simple. Replacing Perspective takes a single API call, and Hindsight catches the Coded Language that similar tools were never built to see.
Gebert’s suggested path is to run Hindsight and Perspective side by side for a week, then look at the delta where they disagreed. Those disagreements show where a toxicity score alone may have been falling short.
Hindsight is capping its launch cohort at 4 commercial clients to allow custom calibration of model instances against each platform’s unique community policies and risk profile. Founder pricing will be offered to that first group.
To join the launch list and test Hindsight with your data, visit https://hindsightAI.com.
