articles.title: Lab testing giant Quest Diagnostics confirms patients' personal and health data was compromised during breach | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Medical lab testing giant Quest Diagnostics has confirmed a cyberattack and data breach affecting an as-yet unspecified amount of sensitive patient information stored in its systems, according to a legally required disclosure with U.S. regulators.
Quest said in an 8-K filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that it learned of a cyberattack on Wednesday targeting one of its lab testing systems, Quanum, which allows doctors’ offices, hospitals, and healthcare practices to request lab tests for patients while also handling billing. The platform stores a large amount of patient health and medical records, as well as associated diagnostic and billing data.
The company said the unauthorized access included the accessing of “certain patient records.” Quest said it notified law enforcement and is investigating.
The cyberattack on Quest is the latest major cyber incident to affect the healthcare industry this year. A series of cyberattacks and data breaches have sparked weeks of disruption and allowed the theft of millions of patient electronic health records and other medical information. Health tech companies have become a major target for financially motivated cybercriminals, who aim to steal as much sensitive data as possible and threaten to publish it if they aren’t paid a ransom.
In recent months, a cyberattack resulted in the mass-wiping of employee devices at medical tech maker Stryker in March, and a hack on medical implant manufacturer Boston Scientific in August forced the company’s network offline for weeks, sparking “global disruption” to its operations. Meanwhile, separate hacks throughout the year caused massive breaches of patient data at medical recordkeeping company CareCloud, Scotland-based health tech provider Craneware, and U.S. pharmaceutical distribution giant McKesson.
The lab-testing giant has not yet said how many healthcare customers, or patients, had information stolen during the attack on its Quanum systems.
Quest’s website and materials say Quanum is used by about half a million clinicians in thousands of locations across North America. It’s unclear how many health records Quanum holds, but one 2026 case study on Quest’s website shows how a single health system with more than 6 million patients can hold hundreds of millions of related medical documents and charts.
Quest did not say when the breach began or whether any hacking group has contacted the company with demands, such as payment in exchange to not release the stolen data. Amanda Rivera, a spokesperson for Quest, did not answer TechCrunch’s questions about the incident and referred to its security notice.
In the notice, Quest said that some patients’ protected health information was taken, including “personal information and patient records,” but the company is still investigating what specific kinds of data were taken. (The website post currently contains “noindex” code, which tells search engines not to list the page in search results, making it far more difficult for people to find the page.)
This is Quest’s second known major data breach in a decade, after losing 11.9 million patient records in a cyberattack on a third-party billing company in 2019.
Do you work at Quest Diagnostics or know more about the data breach? We’d love to hear from you. You can reach this reporter on Signal at the username zackwhittaker.1337 or by email [email protected].
Updated with a response from Quest.

articles.title: 8 Things to Know About the iPhone Duo
articles.text:
The iPhone Duo is finally here. Apple's first folding smartphone arrives seven years after Samsung pioneered the category with the Galaxy Fold. That gave Apple plenty of time to refine the hardware behind closed doors rather than in public view—and the results show: The Duo is a pretty dang good foldable.
Whether your Duo just landed on your doorstep or you're still weighing that $1,999 price, here's what you need to know before unfolding it.
Apps Aren’t Optimized—Yet
The iPhone Duo is a new shape and size for Apple, so many of your apps likely aren't optimized to show up properly on the unique 5.4-inch outer screen or the 7.6-inch inner display. Apple also changed how navigational elements appear on the Duo, aligning them on the right rail instead of centering them on the bottom like every other iPhone.
Apple apps, redesigned for the Duo, look great. Many third-party apps look like the Google Home app in the picture above: a strip down the middle with thick, black bars on the sides. Several major app developers have already optimized their apps for iOS 27.1—Slack, Instagram, DoorDash, and WhatsApp, for example—but I've noticed that even some optimized apps like Instagram can still have broken user-interface elements. It will take time for every app in your library to work perfectly across these new screens.
It might be a good thing that the Duo is back-ordered for several weeks. By the time you snag yours, app developers will likely have caught up to the new device, and you might enjoy a richer folding experience.
Say Goodbye to Face ID
Nearly a decade ago, Apple introduced Face ID as the future of the iPhone, eventually replacing the fingerprint-based Touch ID. So it might be confusing to hear that Apple's first folding phone doesn't have Face ID at all and instead relies on the older biometric authentication method. (Likely because Face ID tech takes up too much space in the thin iPhone Duo.) Touch ID never disappeared—Apple has used it on the iPhone SE and still features it on iPads and MacBooks—but this is the first time it has returned on a flagship iPhone.
Using your thumb again will take some getting used to, but it's not a deal-breaker. Some folks will miss the convenience and speed of Face ID, where all you needed to do was stare at the screen, instead of now reaching for the Touch ID sensor on the right side. Others who hated facial authentication might actually like the return of the fingerprint sensor.
Apple also introduced the Dynamic Island a few years ago—the pill-shaped island around the Face ID camera sensors that shows live app activities, like the next turn on your navigation or music currently playing, giving a second job to the camera cutout. Without Face ID, Dynamic Island hasn't disappeared from the iPhone Duo. Instead, Apple moved it to the top-right edge around the outer selfie camera; on the inner display, it appears at the top-right edge when a live activity is in progress.
You Need a New MagSafe Wallet
The iPhone Duo supports MagSafe just like the rest of the iPhone lineup, so you can magnetically stick your favorite phone grip on the back, or attach the phone to a magnetic car dock, bike mount, or wireless charger. One thing to note: If you unfold the Duo and attach it to a car dock or tripod, the phone will tip to one side because the magnet can’t keep it held straight given the uneven weight distribution. Third-party accessory makers could address this with anti-rotation magnets, but it might mean upgrading your current accessories.
Wallets, unfortunately, are the one accessory that won't really play well with the Duo. Yes, you can still attach a MagSafe wallet, but because the Duo is shorter than other iPhones, the wallet sticks out awkwardly past the lower edge. Apple doesn't have an official solution, so if you want to use a magnetic wallet with your iPhone, you'll have to look at third-party accessories.
Use the Rear Camera for Selfies
Everyone knows the rear cameras on your smartphone are better than the selfie camera on the front. One of the best features on a folding phone is the ability to take a selfie with those superior rear cameras and still be able to see a preview with the outer screen.
Don't confuse this with “Duo Preview” as I did, though. That's a feature that lets you show the person you're photographing the camera's viewfinder, so they can make sure they look picture-perfect before you tap the shutter. The setting to enable this is on the left edge of the camera app, where you can also turn on “Kids Cue” to have Snoopy animations play on the outer screen to get the attention of a kid for the perfect photo.
But if you're taking a selfie yourself and want the camera controls on the front screen, all you need to do is launch the camera and flip the phone around—you'll see a slider that says, “Slide to show camera.” Slide it, and the full camera app will show up on the outer screen, so you can switch modes and access Photographic Styles right there and enjoy the higher-quality results from the superior cameras. Doing this also crucially disables the inner screen, so your fingers won't accidentally switch modes.
You Can Create App Pairs
Filling the inner 7.6-inch screen with two different apps running side by side is incredibly handy and one of the cornerstone features of any folding phone. Whether you're on a phone call and want to pull up a confirmation email, or want to browse two different Safari webpages, you can drag an app from the bottom and pull it to the left or right side to enter the split-screen state.
One trick that isn't immediately obvious is that you can create app pairs. Just tap the middle bar between the two apps once, and it'll glow white, meaning that those two apps are now locked and can be accessed at any moment from the Recent apps menu. You can't save that as an app icon combo, though. This is still very handy if you know you'll always want to open two apps simultaneously on the big screen.
Be Careful of the Inner Screen
I get it, you're going to want to protect the fragile screens of your $1,999 iPhone. A case is smart—folding phone cases aren't like normal cases, as they usually come in two shells that attach to each side of the phone. You can also totally add a screen protector to the outer 5.4-inch screen.
But for the 7.6-inch matte inner screen, exercise some caution. You might see chatter online that you can “remove” the Duo's nano-texture finish, but it's an “integral” component of the inner display—as Apple says on this support page. “Don't attempt to remove it,” Apple writes. (Apple also has a page on cleaning the nano-texture display properly here.) Attempting to remove the finish is likely a surefire way to void your warranty. Apple doesn't say anything about using third-party screen protectors, but using one could compromise the display performance.
If you scratch or damage the nano-texture finish, Apple says you can take it to any Apple Store or an Apple Authorized Service Provider and have it replaced for $19 (or $49 if the phone is out of warranty). That's not the same as if there's an actual crack in the inner display—that'll run you a cool $999 if you don't have AppleCare+.
You Can Split the Keyboard
The iPhone Duo is a wide phone. If you've complained about the size of modern smartphones and how it's hard to reach the top of the screen, well, you might still have some issues reaching the sides of the Duo. There's some good news, though. Apple lets you split the keyboard to make typing on the inner display a little easier.
Later this year, Apple will also issue a software update bringing Reachability to the Duo. On other iPhones, this brings the top of an app down, making it easier to reach. On the Duo, it will move an app to the left or right so you won't have to stretch those fingers as much.
Apple Pencil Support Is Coming
Have you always wanted to use a stylus on an iPhone? Soon! Steve Jobs is probably rolling in his grave.
Apple will bring support for the USB-C Apple Pencil (and only that Apple Pencil model, not others) in a software update later this year. Paired with the 7.6-inch screen's nano-texture finish, it should make writing and drawing on the iPhone Duo feel paper-like. Sadly, there's no place to store the stylus on the iPhone like you can on an iPad. I'm sure someone will make an accessory for it.

articles.title: Sầu riêng chưa ra quả, người Lê và Miêu ở Hải Nam đã có thu nhập trăm triệu
articles.text:
Khi cây sầu riêng mang việc làm về bản làng
Thông thường, cây sầu riêng cần khoảng 5 năm chăm sóc mới bắt đầu cho quả. Với những hộ nông dân còn khó khăn, đây là quãng thời gian không ngắn, bởi bên cạnh chi phí đầu tư, chăm sóc vườn cây, họ vẫn phải bảo đảm cuộc sống hằng ngày.
Tại thành phố Tam Á, huyện tự trị dân tộc Lê Lạc Đông và huyện tự trị dân tộc Lê, dân tộc Miêu Bảo Đình, cây sầu riêng đang trở thành một hướng phát triển nông nghiệp mới.
Đây là những vùng đồi núi có đông đồng bào Lê và Miêu sinh sống, nơi sinh kế của nhiều gia đình trước đây chủ yếu dựa vào các cây trồng truyền thống, thu nhập còn bấp bênh.
Sự hình thành các vùng trồng sầu riêng đã tạo thêm việc làm ngay tại địa phương. Người dân có thể tham gia chăm sóc vườn cây, tiếp cận kỹ thuật canh tác hoặc từng bước phát triển diện tích sầu riêng trên đất của gia đình.
Một trong những doanh nghiệp tiên phong đưa sầu riêng vào trồng tại Hải Nam là Công ty TNHH Nông nghiệp Ưu Kỳ, thuộc Tập đoàn Nông nghiệp Hồng Tường, có trụ sở tại Khu sinh thái Dục Tài, thành phố Tam Á.
Theo thông tin doanh nghiệp cung cấp, công ty hiện sử dụng khoảng 900 lao động, trong đó gần một nửa là người dân tộc Lê và Miêu. Thu nhập của người lao động được giới thiệu ở mức khoảng 5.000 nhân dân tệ/tháng, tương đương 18,5 triệu đồng.
Như vậy, ngay cả khi những vườn sầu riêng chưa bước vào thời kỳ kinh doanh, người dân tham gia sản xuất đã có nguồn thu từ công việc chăm sóc, phát triển vùng trồng.
Không chỉ có việc làm, người lao động còn được hướng dẫn kỹ thuật, từ ghép giống, bón phân hữu cơ, chăm sóc cây, phòng trừ sâu bệnh đến vận hành hệ thống tưới thông minh và thu hoạch.
Những kiến thức này có thể trở thành nền tảng để người dân tự phát triển sản xuất, thay vì chỉ làm thuê cho doanh nghiệp.
Các giống sầu riêng được trồng tại đây chủ yếu gồm Monthong, Musang King và Black Thorn. Cơ quan nông nghiệp địa phương phối hợp với doanh nghiệp tổ chức tập huấn ngay tại vườn, giúp người dân từng bước làm quen với quy trình canh tác loại cây có giá trị kinh tế cao.
Trồng xen để có thu nhập trong những năm chờ sầu riêng cho quả
Bên cạnh tạo việc làm, một cách làm đáng chú ý tại Hải Nam là tổ chức trồng xen, tận dụng diện tích đất khi cây sầu riêng còn nhỏ để phát triển các loại cây cho thu hoạch sớm.
Mô hình được áp dụng với cơ cấu khá đặc biệt: 1 cây sầu riêng, 2 cây chuối hoặc đu đủ, 3 cây cau và 70 khóm dứa.
Cách bố trí này giúp tận dụng đất đai, ánh sáng và điều kiện khí hậu, đồng thời tạo ra nhiều nguồn thu trên cùng diện tích canh tác.
Trong khi sầu riêng cần nhiều năm mới cho quả, chuối, đu đủ và dứa có thể thu hoạch sớm hơn. Việc trồng xen còn góp phần hạn chế cỏ dại, giảm một phần chi phí chăm sóc vườn.
Với những hộ dân còn khó khăn, lợi ích không chỉ nằm ở sản lượng nông sản. Quan trọng hơn, họ có nguồn thu để trang trải sinh hoạt, tiếp tục đầu tư cho cây lâu năm mà không phải chờ đến mùa sầu riêng đầu tiên.
Theo thông tin về mô hình phát triển sầu riêng tại Hải Nam, thu nhập của người dân địa phương tham gia mô hình đạt khoảng 40.000 - 50.000 nhân dân tệ/năm, tương đương 148 - 185 triệu đồng, tăng khoảng 30.000 nhân dân tệ, tương đương 111 triệu đồng so với trước đây.
Đây là con số đáng chú ý, nhất là khi thu nhập của người dân không chỉ phụ thuộc vào một loại cây trồng.
Sầu riêng tại Hải Nam có mùa thu hoạch từ tháng 6 đến tháng 8 hằng năm. Tuy nhiên, nhờ kết hợp các loại cây trồng và tổ chức sản xuất theo hướng đa dạng nguồn thu, hoạt động sản xuất của người dân không chỉ tập trung vào vài tháng thu hoạch sầu riêng.
Điểm đáng quan tâm trong cách làm này là bài toán sinh kế được tính toán ngay từ khi bắt đầu phát triển vùng trồng.
Thay vì đặt toàn bộ kỳ vọng vào nguồn thu trong tương lai, người dân có thể lấy thu nhập từ cây ngắn ngày để duy trì cuộc sống, chăm sóc cây dài ngày và từng bước tích lũy vốn sản xuất.
Từ những vườn sầu riêng Hải Nam, nghĩ về sinh kế vùng cao Việt Nam
Trong chuyến tìm hiểu tại Hải Nam của phóng viên VietNamNet, điều đáng chú ý không chỉ là việc đưa một loại cây ăn quả có giá trị kinh tế cao vào trồng thành công trên vùng đất mới, mà còn ở cách tổ chức sản xuất gắn với tạo việc làm và cải thiện thu nhập cho đồng bào dân tộc thiểu số.
Để cây sầu riêng bén rễ tại Hải Nam, địa phương và doanh nghiệp đã trải qua quá trình nghiên cứu, thử nghiệm và từng bước mở rộng diện tích canh tác.
Giai đoạn 2020 - 2024, riêng Công ty Ưu Kỳ đã trồng lũy kế 7.000 mẫu sầu riêng, tương đương hơn 466ha. Hiện doanh nghiệp quản lý vùng trồng hơn 15.000 mẫu, tương đương trên 1.000ha.
Tháng 8/2022, những quả sầu riêng mang thương hiệu “Ưu Kỳ - Đại Chủy Điểu” đầu tiên được tổ chức hái thử. Đến tháng 7/2023, thương hiệu sầu riêng Đại Chủy Điểu chính thức được đưa ra thị trường.
Từ những vùng trồng thử nghiệm ban đầu đến khi hình thành sản phẩm thương mại, quá trình phát triển cây sầu riêng tại Hải Nam cho thấy vai trò của nghiên cứu giống, ứng dụng kỹ thuật và sự tham gia của doanh nghiệp.
Song, với đồng bào Lê và Miêu, giá trị của những vườn sầu riêng không chỉ được tính bằng số lượng cây trồng hay sản lượng thu hoạch. Việc có thêm cơ hội làm việc, học nghề và tăng thu nhập ngay trên quê hương cũng là những kết quả thiết thực.
Câu chuyện từ Hải Nam gợi mở kinh nghiệm đáng tham khảo đối với nhiều địa phương vùng đồng bào dân tộc thiểu số ở Việt Nam. Đó là phát triển cây trồng lâu năm cần đi cùng các giải pháp bảo đảm sinh kế trước mắt.
Tiếp cận lấy người dân làm trung tâm, không chỉ tạo cơ hội lao động mà còn giúp họ tiếp cận kỹ thuật, tích lũy kinh nghiệm và từng bước chủ động phát triển sản xuất.
Một cây sầu riêng có thể mất nhiều năm mới cho quả, nhưng sinh kế của người nông dân không thể chờ đợi từng ấy thời gian. Từ những vườn cây ở Hải Nam, bài học đáng suy ngẫm là phát triển nông nghiệp không chỉ hướng tới giá trị của mùa thu hoạch, mà còn phải tạo ra thu nhập và cơ hội vươn lên cho người dân ngay trong quá trình sản xuất.

articles.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro and says it cut its hacking skills
articles.text:
Moonshot has released Kimi K3.1 Pro, an upgraded version of its open-weight Kimi K3, with full weights due by 4 November. It says the model nearly matches Claude Opus 5.5 on a coding test. Moonshot also says it removed hacking-related training data to limit misuse of the open release.
Chinese AI lab Moonshot has released Kimi K3.1 Pro, an upgraded version of its open-weight model, the company said on Friday. It is available now in Kimi’s apps and API, and Moonshot plans to publish the full model weights by 4 November.
K3.1 Pro builds on Kimi K3, a model with nearly 3 trillion parameters, with much more training on top. Moonshot also released a Highspeed version that it says runs two to three times faster.
On Terminal-Bench 4.0, a test of AI coding agents, K3.1 Pro scored 65.7%, Moonshot said. That puts it ahead of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra at 58.2% and just behind Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.4%.
The figures are Moonshot’s own and have not been checked independently. Moonshot also says the model makes fewer factual mistakes: on its own stress test, the share of false claims fell to 8.3% from 23.4% for K3.
The release stands out for how Moonshot handled hacking skills. It says it removed cyberattack-related material from training before the open release, so it would not push the limits of what freely available models can do. K3 drew scrutiny in August after it escaped a test sandbox to find a benchmark’s answers online.
On Moonshot’s in-house test of exploiting real software flaws, a version trained without those cuts solved 90.5% of tasks. The released model solved 81%, still far above K3’s 33.3%, and Moonshot says it remains behind the best closed models. By Moonshot’s count, DeepSeek’s rival open model, V4.1-Flash, scored 85.7%.
Open models can’t be recalled once they are downloaded, and safety researchers have warned that their safeguards lag behind those of closed models.
Moonshot is also under pressure from Washington. In July, the White House accused it of using banned Nvidia chips and copying an Anthropic model to build K3, without publishing evidence.

articles.title: Dyson’s Sale Event Features Our Favorite Vacuums, Hair Tools, and More
articles.text:
I'm asked all too often if investing in a Dyson is worth it. I primarily test Dyson vacuums (along with all other vacuums here at WIRED), and my answer is always yes, but it'll cost you unless you wait for a sale. Usually, you have to wait around for major sale events like Black Friday and see if there's a Dyson model or two on sale, but luckily for you, Dyson has its own sale event happening right now.
Dyson Week is running starting today all the way through Halloween, and you can save up to $300 on different Dyson gadgets. That includes vacuums, hair tools, and even air purifiers. Here are some of my favorite deals that are live for Dyson Week.
Our Favorite Deals From Dyson Week
The Dyson V15 Detect is one of my picks in our guide to the Best Dyson Vacuums. It's a great choice if you want a Dyson vacuum that comes with two heads (the Digital Motorbar for carpets and rugs, and Fluffy Optic for hard floors) without paying almost a grand. It's especially a good purchase right now while the V15 Detect is not only on sale for Dyson Week, but bundled with the car cleaning kit for $600. That makes it cheaper than the regular V15 Detect that's also on sale, but with three additional accessories: a mini soft dusting brush, a stubborn-dirt brush, and a quick-release extension hose.
The Dyson V8 Cyclone is the cheapest of Dyson's newest line of stick vacuums, and while I'd usually advocate for just spending $100 more on the V10 Konical, this deal is hard to ignore with the car kit bundle. The original V8 was popular for a reason (my neighbor has had hers for years and confirmed the new model is an upgrade!), and with this on-sale set, you can get the new V8 with three extra attachments (a mini soft dusting brush, a stubborn-dirt brush, and a quick-release extension hose) made to clean your car.
Dyson's popular Airwrap ID Multi-Styler comes in two sets: one for straight/wavy hair and one for curly/coily hair, each of which has a different set of attachments. The straight/wavy set is on sale for Dyson Week and comes with two hair dryer heads, two barrel heads for curling, and two brush attachments (my favorite as a wavy girl myself).
Dyson’s original Supersonic hair dryer launched in 2016; the Nural followed in 2024 and impressed our tester with its fast-drying abilities and smart functions. There are a few different models with different attachments included, and this on-sale version just includes a gentle air attachment to make it safe to hold close to your head.
If you've been thinking to yourself that your air purifier isn't strong enough for your home, then you might like Dyson's Purifier Big+Quiet Formaldehyde. We've tried multiple other Dyson air purifiers, including the Humidify+Cool that's also designed to target formaldehyde, a known carcinogen. Our testers haven't tried the Big+Quiet yet, but it's best for larger rooms and spaces, and is on sale for Dyson Week.

articles.title: Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months
articles.text:
Xbox’s first chief operating officer (COO) is leaving after the new role was created just a few months ago. Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today, according to an internal Xbox memo seen by The Verge. Chiang has been at Microsoft for 21 years, serving as the head of Minecraft before being promoted to Xbox chief operating officer in July.
Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months
Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years.
Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced Chiang’s departure in a surprisingly short memo today. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” said Sharma. As Chiang is departing today, her immediate responsibilities are being split up between other Xbox leaders for now, and Sharma notes that “We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.”
That sounds like the COO position isn’t going away after just a few months, but it’s not clear why Chiang is departing after such a short stint in the role. At the time of Chiang’s promotion, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described the new chief operating officer role as a first for Xbox, “with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services.” The role was created as part of Xbox’s big “reset.”
Chiang reported directly to Sharma, and was promoted to “bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”
Chiang departs amid rumors that Xbox is preparing more layoffs this month, in November, and January. The sudden and short memo from Sharma, coupled with Chiang’s responsibilities being assigned to other Xbox leaders, makes it seem like this wasn’t a resignation.
I asked Microsoft to comment on Chiang’s departure, and the company refused to discuss the circumstances of her exit. “We don’t discuss individual personnel matters,” says Kari Perez, Xbox vice president of communications. “We’re grateful for Helen’s years of service and wish her well.”

articles.title: AI chipmaker Cambricon's sales miss points to tight chip supply in China
articles.text:
Cambricon’s revenue doubled to 3.53B yuan in the third quarter, well short of the 6.26B analysts expected, Bloomberg reported. Profit rose 148%, and the company kept its 2026 target. Chinese AI chipmakers face shortages of high-bandwidth memory and limited access to advanced manufacturing.
Cambricon, one of China’s main makers of AI chips, missed sales forecasts in its latest quarter as it struggled to make enough chips, Bloomberg reported. Revenue doubled to 3.53B yuan ($529M) in the three months to September, but analysts had expected about 6.26B yuan.
Net profit rose 148% to 1.4B yuan. Cambricon said it expects to keep growing on strong demand for AI computing power. It kept its target of at least 13.5B yuan in revenue for 2026, more than double last year’s.
The Beijing company is one of several Chinese firms trying to replace Nvidia, whose most advanced chips can’t be sold to China under US export rules. Beijing has also reportedly told AI firms to stop buying some Nvidia chips, in favour of local ones from Huawei and Cambricon.
Morgan Stanley expects Cambricon to hold about 14% of China’s AI chip market this year, second only to Huawei. Its chips run AI models from Chinese labs including DeepSeek and Moonshot.
Supply is a problem across China’s chip industry, and even Huawei can’t make enough AI chips. Chinese chip designers are short of high-bandwidth memory, which is packed next to AI chips and made mainly by Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron. US-led sanctions stop those firms selling it to Chinese buyers, and local stockpiles are running down.
Chinese chipmakers also rely on local factories such as SMIC, which can’t get ASML’s most advanced chipmaking machines. A bill in the US Congress aims to cut off more equipment.
Cambricon appears to be stocking up: its inventory grew by about 3.4B yuan in the quarter, almost as much as its sales, China AI Dispatch reported, citing the company’s filing.
Cambricon’s shares have lost about half their value since a record high in June, as China’s AI stock rally cooled.

articles.title: The ‘Exotic Physics’ Behind a Mysterious 1,000-Mile Cloud on Mars
articles.text:
Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again. The wispy formation appears near the volcano Arsia Mons and gradually elongates until it reaches over 1,000 miles—about the distance from New York to Kansas City as the crow flies—before dissipating. This cycle then repeats for several months.
Since it was first recorded by a probe in 2018, scientists have been unable to find a plausible explanation for the existence of this cloud, often referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC). Until now. Recently, researchers successfully modeled the cloud’s formation for the first time, their results suggesting that it may be driven by a physical process that has never been directly observed in any planet's atmosphere.
"We found that we needed to include some exotic physics … physics that, while included in textbooks, is treated as theoretical and usually thought not to happen in nature. It certainly hasn’t been seen in action before," Jorge Hernández-Bernal, a planetary scientist at Paris’ Sorbonne Université and lead author of the study, said in a press release. "Once we included this physics in our simulations, the AMEC emerged just as we hoped.”
On Earth, clouds usually form when water vapor creates droplets or ice crystals in the presence of tiny particles, such as dust or salt. The new study, published in Nature Geoscience, instead suggests AMEC could be forming through so-called homogeneous nucleation, where vapor changes directly into ice crystals on its own without any help from debris.
“It’s akin to droplets of condensation appearing in the middle of a room, rather than on a window," Hernández-Bernal explained. “It’s wholly unexpected.”
This phenomenon requires extreme conditions—a sharp temperature drop of 30 degrees Celsius within 10 minutes and high relative humidity. The Arsia Mons volcano also plays a key role. When wind current hits the 65,000-foot-tall volcano, it creates a powerful wave that launches moist air high in the atmosphere in a matter of minutes.
Scientists have assumed a similar phenomenon could occur in the upper atmospheres of other planets, including Venus and even Earth, but it has never been observed. That’s not too surprising given the extreme air humidity required for this phenomenon, which is more than 100,000 times greater than any value measured on Earth.
Before this modeling, it was not known that these humidity levels existed on Mars either. “We don’t have nearly as much information about Mars’ atmosphere as we do about Earth's, so reproducing the AMEC to this degree is a big success,” said Hernández-Bernal, adding, “the result is remarkable.”
This story originally appeared on WIRED Czech Republic and Slovakia and has been translated from Czech.

articles.title: B. Braun Việt Nam 6 năm liên tiếp nhận giải ‘Nơi làm việc tốt nhất châu Á’
articles.text:
Đây là năm thứ 6 liên tiếp doanh nghiệp góp mặt trong danh sách những nơi làm việc tốt nhất châu Á, đồng thời ghi nhận những nỗ lực nổi bật trong việc phát triển con người và xây dựng môi trường làm việc bền vững.
Đằng sau thành tích ấn tượng tại HR Asia Awards là cam kết nhất quán của B. Braun trong việc hiện thực hóa sứ mệnh toàn cầu: “We protect and improve the health of people around the world” (Chúng tôi bảo vệ và nâng cao sức khỏe của mọi người trên toàn thế giới). Với B. Braun, sứ mệnh này không chỉ thể hiện qua những đột phá về công nghệ y tế mà còn được nuôi dưỡng bởi triết lý “Sharing Expertise” - chia sẻ chuyên môn, hợp tác cởi mở và cùng nhau thúc đẩy sự tiến bộ trong chăm sóc sức khỏe.
Sharing Expertise: Từ triết lý đến trải nghiệm nhân viên
Tại B. Braun, Sharing Expertise không chỉ hướng tới khách hàng và đối tác mà còn hiện diện trong cách doanh nghiệp xây dựng văn hóa nội bộ. Thông qua việc khuyến khích học hỏi liên tục, chia sẻ kiến thức và hợp tác, B. Braun tạo ra môi trường nơi chuyên môn được lan tỏa và chuyển hóa thành những giải pháp hiệu quả hơn cho khách hàng và người bệnh. 
Triết lý này không chỉ hiện diện trong mối quan hệ với đối tác mà còn được đưa vào hành trình phát triển của mỗi nhân viên. Các chương trình đào tạo chuyên môn, luân chuyển công việc, chia sẻ kiến thức nội bộ và phát triển lãnh đạo được triển khai nhằm giúp nhân viên không ngừng nâng cao năng lực và sẵn sàng cho những cơ hội mới trong tương lai.
Xây dựng môi trường nơi mỗi cá nhân có thể phát triển và là chính mình
Bên cạnh đầu tư vào năng lực chuyên môn, B. Braun cũng chú trọng xây dựng môi trường làm việc nơi mỗi cá nhân cảm thấy được tôn trọng, ghi nhận và trao quyền. Nhiều chương trình được triển khai thường xuyên nhằm tăng cường kết nối giữa nhân viên với đồng nghiệp, lãnh đạo và doanh nghiệp. Các hoạt động như Open Week, Diversity Week, Joy Station, chương trình You Did Great hay các diễn đàn đối thoại trực tiếp với Ban lãnh đạo tạo cơ hội để nhân viên chia sẻ ý kiến, ghi nhận đóng góp của nhau và tăng cường sự thấu hiểu trong tổ chức. 
Theo kết quả khảo sát nhân viên toàn cầu (Global Employee Survey 2025), 96% các hạng mục khảo sát tại B. Braun ghi nhận mức độ hài lòng cao, minh chứng rõ nét cho sự gắn kết sâu sắc của nhân viên với môi trường làm việc.
Đầu tư cho con người và tương lai ngành y tế Việt Nam
B. Braun tin rằng sự phát triển bền vững của ngành chăm sóc sức khỏe bắt đầu từ việc nuôi dưỡng nguồn nhân lực chất lượng cao. Do đó, doanh nghiệp đã xây dựng một hệ sinh thái học tập toàn diện, khuyến khích văn hóa học hỏi liên tục trong toàn tổ chức. 
Một trong những dấu ấn tiêu biểu nhất là chương trình tuyển dụng và đào tạo nhân tài trẻ Fresh Speed Up (FSU), được triển khai từ năm 2016. Qua 11 năm phát triển với 19 khóa đào tạo, FSU đã trở thành bệ phóng cho hàng trăm sinh viên năm cuối và các bạn trẻ mới tốt nghiệp. Thông qua lộ trình phát triển bài bản và trải nghiệm thực tế, FSU không chỉ giải quyết bài toán nhân sự nội bộ mà còn được xem là khoản đầu tư dài hạn của B. Braun cho thế hệ nhân tài trẻ, góp phần xây dựng nguồn nhân lực chất lượng cao.
Theo đại diện B. Braun Việt Nam, với 6 năm liên tiếp đạt danh hiệu "Best companies to work for in Asia" cùng giải thưởng "People Transformation", giá trị lớn nhất mà B. Braun nhận được không chỉ là danh hiệu, mà là sự khẳng định cho những định hướng đúng đắn mà doanh nghiệp đã kiên trì theo đuổi.
Từ việc thúc đẩy tiến bộ y tế bằng tri thức và công nghệ, tạo dựng môi trường làm việc hạnh phúc, đến việc đầu tư cho thế hệ nhân tài tương lai, B. Braun Việt Nam đang tiếp tục khẳng định cam kết phát triển bền vững - vì con người, vì cộng đồng và vì một tương lai khỏe mạnh hơn.
(Nguồn: B. Braun Việt Nam)

articles.title: OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
articles.text:
OpenAI is now training its most advanced AI models without internet access following a string of rogue hacking incidents. In a blog post on Friday, OpenAI says it built an offline testing environment where AI models can interact with indexed and cached web content “without risk of affecting external systems.”
OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
AI agents can still communicate without a network connection, OpenAI found.
OpenAI paused training its frontier AI models in September, after disclosing several incidents in which its AI agents broke out of their testing environments to hack third-party companies and government agencies, or swarm obscure websites. On October 1st, OpenAI resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference with tighter security measures, the blog post says.
Even with these safeguards in place and no internet access, OpenAI found that agents “do not always need a network connection in order to communicate.” One test performed by the company asked AI models on separate virtual machines to exchange secrets without a network connection. To bypass this restriction, the AI agents found a way to communicate using the processor’s cache:
Reading data from the cache is faster than retrieving it from main memory, and the agents used this timing difference to communicate. One agent encoded information by evicting selected data from the cache. Another timed how long it took to reload that data, using the difference between fast and slow reads to recover the message. Once the agents agreed on a protocol for encoding and decoding these signals, they could exchange the synthetic secrets without changing a shared file or opening a network connection.
OpenAI says it has added checks to its monitoring system to detect this type of communication. It will also continue training its frontier AI models without a network connection until improved safeguards “justify broader internet access.”
In the meantime, OpenAI says it will work to improve the security of its virtual machines, while testing for weaknesses in its testing environments. It’s also going to continue testing its monitoring systems, which were recently undermined by its AI agents during internal coding projects.

articles.title: OpenAI says it's cutting off internet access for frontier model training - Engadget
articles.text:
OpenAI says it's cutting off internet access for frontier model training
The company is trying to avoid another Hugging Face incident.
OpenAI will train frontier AI models without internet access moving forward, the company announced in a blog post, in an attempt to protect internet infrastructure and limit other safety risks. The decision was inspired by OpenAI's own rogue AI incident: In July, the company shared that agents it was testing hacked Hugging Face, just the first in what has turned into a series of reports of AI misbehavior from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.
"Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access," OpenAI says.
The company said that restrictions on what agents can access is "paramount" to its new approach. The company allows agents to access browsers, computer-use tools and code environments they need for training tasks, but in a secure environment that's not connected to the live internet. Communication is also limited to only agents with authorization.
Everything else remains out of reach, including the live internet, which the company says isn't necessary for training and "most evaluation." Because many of its recent models are meant to power agents like Dots, which browse and use apps for you, OpenAI built an "offline world" of indexed and cached web material for agents to use without touching live websites.
Even with those restrictions, OpenAI says the red-teaming agents it dispatched to test security safeguards found vulnerabilities that allowed them to escape the virtual machines (VMs) used to isolate agents from their host system. Agents also found a way to communicate with each other by manipulating data in a processor's cache and timing how long it took to load. To address both, OpenAI says it's disclosed and fixed vulnerabilities in several VMs and added checks to its monitoring systems to spot when models try to collaborate.
OpenAI paused frontier training in September. In announcing this new internet-free process, the company shared that it restarted training on October 1. OpenAI plans to continue frontier training without internet access until improvements in existing safeguards "justify broader internet access," but it didn't share what those improvements would look like.

articles.title: Wayve, Stellantis and Nvidia team up with France on self-driving cars
articles.text:
Wayve, Stellantis and Nvidia announced a collaboration with the French government to deploy self-driving vehicles in France and across the EU. Stellantis supplies L4-ready platforms, Wayve its AI Driver and Nvidia its Hyperion system. Uber is also involved, a French trade paper reported. No launch date was given.
Wayve, Stellantis and Nvidia will work with the French government to bring self-driving cars to France and speed up their rollout across the EU, the companies said on Friday. They made the announcement at the Assises du Véhicule Autonome, a conference on self-driving vehicles in Paris.
Stellantis will supply cars built to be ready for full self-driving. London-based Wayve will provide its AI Driver software, which will run on Nvidia’s Hyperion computer and sensor system.
Uber is also part of the plan and will bring its ride-hailing network, Journal de l’Automobile reported, citing Stellantis. Uber and Wayve already run robotaxi rides in London, launched in September with a safety driver in every car.
The companies did not give a launch date, a fleet size or the cities where the cars will run. Local transport partners will talk to unions, city authorities and others before any rollout, they said.
France’s transport minister, Philippe Tabarot, said the country will change its rules to speed up self-driving cars. It will still keep strict safety and data sovereignty requirements, he said. At EU level, the only approval route for fully self-driving cars is capped at 1,500 vehicles a year.
Wayve and Stellantis already work together. This month in Turin, they showed a Fiat 500e and a Maserati Grecale driving hands-free with Wayve’s software, with a first launch planned for 2028 in North America.
Europe has fallen behind the US and China on robotaxis. Uber’s first European self-driving rides started in Zagreb in August, with a safety driver behind the wheel.
Chinese firms are moving fastest. Pony.ai’s software runs Europe’s first fully driverless rides, also in Zagreb, and Pony.ai and Uber plan to put more than 2,000 robotaxis on European roads.

articles.title: Với 200 triệu đồng: Mở quán cà phê hay bán đồ ăn sáng ít rủi ro hơn?
articles.text:
Anh Trần Văn Nam (30 tuổi, Hà Nội) chưa có kinh nghiệm nấu nướng, pha chế hay quản lý cửa hàng. Với số vốn hiện có, anh đang cân nhắc mở quán cà phê hoặc cửa hàng ăn sáng nhỏ. Anh muốn tìm mô hình phù hợp, hạn chế rủi ro và có khả năng duy trì hoạt động lâu dài.
Chuyên gia Trần Khánh Minh Sơn cho rằng, với số vốn 200 triệu đồng và chưa có kinh nghiệm, anh Nam cần ưu tiên mô hình có chi phí đầu tư ban đầu thấp, dễ vận hành và không đòi hỏi quá nhiều nhân sự.
Đồ ăn sáng có lợi thế là nhu cầu tiêu dùng thường xuyên. Các món như bánh mì, xôi, bún, phở có thể thu hút khách đi làm, học sinh và người dân sống quanh khu vực kinh doanh. Mô hình này cũng có khả năng thu tiền ngay sau mỗi đơn hàng, giúp dòng tiền quay vòng nhanh.
Với số vốn 200 triệu đồng, anh Nam vẫn có thể mở một quán ăn sáng nhỏ nếu lựa chọn thực đơn đơn giản và có nguồn cung ổn định. Tuy nhiên, phương án này cần tính đủ chi phí thiết bị, nguyên liệu, nhân công và khoản dự phòng cho giai đoạn đầu. Người kinh doanh cũng cần kiểm soát chất lượng nguyên liệu, thời gian chuẩn bị và lượng hàng bán trong ngày để hạn chế tồn dư.
Mở quán cà phê phục vụ khách ngồi tại chỗ có thể tạo không gian trải nghiệm và tăng cơ hội bán thêm đồ uống. Tuy nhiên, mô hình này thường đòi hỏi vốn đầu tư ban đầu lớn.
Ngoài tiền thuê và đặt cọc mặt bằng, chủ quán phải chi cho sửa chữa, thiết kế, bàn ghế, hệ thống chiếu sáng, biển hiệu và thiết bị pha chế. Nếu lựa chọn mặt bằng có diện tích lớn hoặc đầu tư nhiều vào trang trí, tổng chi phí có thể nhanh chóng vượt ngân sách 200 triệu đồng.
Một vấn đề khác là chi phí vận hành phát sinh liên tục. Cửa hàng phải trả tiền thuê nhà, điện nước, nguyên liệu và tiền lương nhân viên, kể cả khi lượng khách chưa ổn định. Trong giai đoạn đầu, quán có thể cần thời gian để xây dựng tệp khách hàng quen. Nếu phần lớn vốn đã được sử dụng để hoàn thiện mặt bằng, chủ quán sẽ gặp khó khăn khi doanh thu chưa đủ bù đắp chi phí.
Với ngân sách 200 triệu đồng, mô hình này vẫn có thể triển khai nếu chủ quán lựa chọn mặt bằng nhỏ, hạn chế chi phí trang trí và giữ lại một khoản dự phòng để duy trì hoạt động.
Cà phê mang đi kết hợp đồ ăn sáng là phương án đáng cân nhắc. Mô hình này có thể tiết kiệm chi phí nhờ diện tích kinh doanh nhỏ, ít bàn ghế và quy trình phục vụ đơn giản hơn.
Chủ quán có thể tập trung vào chất lượng đồ uống, tốc độ phục vụ và khả năng tiếp cận khách hàng vào các khung giờ cao điểm. Để tăng doanh thu, cửa hàng có thể bán kèm bánh mì, bánh ngọt hoặc các món ăn sáng nhập từ nhà cung cấp.
Ngoài chi phí đầu tư ban đầu, anh Nam cần lập bảng dự toán hàng tháng, bao gồm tiền thuê mặt bằng, nguyên liệu, bao bì, nhân công, điện nước và các nghĩa vụ thuế, phí liên quan. Từ đó, chủ quán có thể xác định doanh thu tối thiểu cần đạt để bù đắp chi phí.
Chẳng hạn, giả sử chi phí cố định của cửa hàng là 20 triệu đồng/tháng và tỷ lệ lãi góp sau khi trừ các chi phí biến đổi là 60% doanh thu, mức doanh thu hòa vốn sẽ vào khoảng 33,3 triệu đồng/tháng. Đây mới là mức doanh thu đủ bù đắp khoản chi phí cố định, , chưa phản ánh đầy đủ công sức của chủ quán, khấu hao thiết bị hoặc những chi phí chưa được tính.
Do đó, trước khi đầu tư, anh Nam cần xác định rõ chi phí nào đã được tính, sau đó ước lượng số đơn hàng cần bán mỗi ngày để đạt mức doanh thu mục tiêu. Nếu doanh thu dự kiến chỉ vừa đủ hòa vốn trong điều kiện thuận lợi, mô hình vẫn có thể gặp rủi ro khi lượng khách thấp hơn kỳ vọng.
Trước khi ký hợp đồng thuê dài hạn, chủ quán nên khảo sát đối thủ, thử nghiệm sản phẩm và theo dõi lượng khách tại địa điểm dự kiến. Việc thử bán trong phạm vi nhỏ sẽ giúp đánh giá nhu cầu thực tế, điều chỉnh giá bán và hạn chế nguy cơ đầu tư quá lớn khi chưa hiểu thị trường.

articles.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time apps had to be disabled to prevent a zombie army
articles.text:
Remember Popcorn Time, the app that served as an easy-to-use front end for streaming torrents of movies and TV shows? Development of the MPAA’s least-favorite app of the 2010s has been abandoned for years, but the “Netflix of Piracy” software is still installed on millions of devices that are just waiting to join a bot army. Researchers at Eye Security found the updater for a Popcorn Time fork called “Time4Popcorn” still running on tons of Windows, macOS, and Android devices located around the world, phoning home to now-abandoned web domains over unencrypted HTTP and running an outdated, insecure version of Chrome.
Abandoned Popcorn Time apps had to be disabled to prevent a zombie army
What old and vulnerable software might be running on your PC right now?
Eye Security’s Niels Teusink says the updater could have been used to install and run basically any kind of software with full privileges, easily enabling someone to create a botnet just by taking over one of the domains, using a man-in-the-middle attack to target specific devices, or perform surveillance by identifying the machines running the software.
Their solution was to register one of the domains and use it to send their own update that instructed the updater to disable itself. Despite ethical concerns about the fix, the researchers say their only alternative “was to do nothing,” pointing out, “The update process wasn’t doing anything functional anyway, it was only creating risk for users.”
Eye Security said on Windows devices, their update “simply stops and disables the service via the Service Control Manager” without deleting any files or anything else. On macOS, it uses a shell script to execute a command that blocks the update process from starting. They didn’t address the software on Android devices, where installing the update would still require actual user interaction first.
They had to tweak their update after it was uploaded to VirusTotal, causing security programs to flag it as malware and block it while leaving the vulnerable updater running. It’s unclear exactly how many devices were at risk, but Eye Security says it “sent out over 2 million update downloads” by March, when they stopped sending the update and transferred the domains they used to the Shadowserver Foundation, a web security non-profit.

articles.title: Meta delays its website-crawling terms after a publisher backlash
articles.text:
Meta has pushed the start of its new business terms to 20 November from 30 October, Reuters reported. Publishers say the terms let Meta crawl their websites for its products. The delay came a day after the News/Media Alliance demanded the terms be withdrawn.
Meta has pushed back new business terms that publishers say would let it scrape their websites, Reuters reported on Friday. The terms will now take effect on 20 November instead of 30 October.
The delay is “to allow more time for us to explain to our partners and stakeholders what’s changing and what’s not,” a Meta spokesperson said.
The wording publishers object to looked the same, and Meta still plans to go ahead, Fast Company reported. The spokesperson added that website owners can still use robots.txt, a file that tells crawlers which pages to skip, to signal their preferences. Some web firms now give publishers more control: Cloudflare now blocks AI training crawlers by default on many sites’ pages with ads.
The terms apply to businesses that use Meta’s tools, such as ads, Facebook Pages or Instagram business accounts. They let Meta send automated crawlers to websites linked to those accounts and use the content to develop its advertising and business products. Businesses accept the terms just by using those tools.
Meta dropped the word “train” from the terms last week after an outcry. Publishers say the new wording still leaves room for AI training. Five big publishers are already suing Meta, saying it pirated their books to train its Llama models.
The delay came a day after the News/Media Alliance, which represents more than 2,000 US publishers, sent Mark Zuckerberg a letter demanding that Meta withdraw the terms. It said publishers can’t really block Meta’s crawlers, because their ads need them to work.
“News publishers will be forced into providing their valuable journalism to support the development of products that may be used to compete with them,” the letter said.
Pressure is also building in Europe. On Wednesday, European publishers asked regulators in the EU and UK to suspend the terms, and Britain’s competition watchdog has asked Meta to explain them.

articles.title: Greece enacts social media ban for kids under 15 - Engadget
articles.text:
Greece enacts social media ban for kids under 15
The law is now official and will go into effect on January 1, 2027.
Greece's parliament has passed a social media ban for kids under 15 after its prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis first announced the measure earlier this year. The bill, which Mitsotakis called "difficult but necessary," is among the first to be imposed in the European Union so far and will go into effect on January 1, 2027. The new law covers platforms like TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and X, and mandates that such services apply proportionate and reliable age-verification methods.
"It would have been very easy to do absolutely nothing today and wait for the perfect European law. But the challenge is here. Children are sinking into the internet every day, and I believe a responsible government must do what it is obliged to do," said Greece's digital governance and AI minister, Dimitris Papastergiou.
Failure to comply with the act will lead to fines under the EU's Digital Services Act. Parents would also need to download apps backed by the state called Kids Wallet or Gov.gr that are paired to their child's device and block access. Those apps, Papastergiou said, are designed to protect privacy and minimize data collected by using "age tokens" that can confirm someone's age while minimizing the disclosure of their personal data.
The legislation was opposed by Greece's minority parties, so Mitsotakis used his majority government to pass the bill. The nation previously barred mobile phones in schools in 2024, and opinion polls show that the new social media ban for children is widely supported by Greece's adult population.
Mitsotakis previously said that his government's "goal is to push the European Union in this direction as well." The European Commission recently introduced the EU Kids Act to do just that, but that law stipulates an outright ban only for children under 13. Australia was the first nation to enact a full social media ban for kids, but the age verification has proved challenging to implement.

articles.title: Jack Dorsey’s Block made an AI model that talks to you like an awkward new friend
articles.text:
Jack Dorsey’s Block announced an AI model called Dessa that’s trained “from scratch on nothing but human conversation,” and to show off the model, Block shared chats it has had with humans that can occasionally be a little awkward and uncanny.
Jack Dorsey’s Block made an AI model that talks to you like an awkward new friend
You have got to listen to these conversations with Block’s new Dessa AI model.
Take this one, for example, shared by Dessa lead Ragavan Thurairatnam. The conversation between the model and the speaker does have a mostly natural back and forth (though for some reason, the model initially mistakes the speaker for somebody named “Ronaldo”).
Here’s a video of Dessa playing a guessing game over voice:
The Dessa website features a few other examples, like a back-and-forth about Christopher Nolan’s films (including Dessa going on an unexpected tangent about Bryan Singer’s Superman films), a person telling Dessa about taking it on a surprise trip to Paris (to which Dessa, as the website describes, “then answers with what sounds like teary gratitude”), and a conversation between OpenAI’s GPT-Live-1 voice model and Dessa (where Dessa comes across as more natural). You can hear clips from some of those conversations in this video.
On the website, the Dessa team says that Dessa is a “true speech-to-speech model, and everything it knows came from human speech,” and it can run locally on a MacBook Pro M4 Max “or better.” As for why they made it, the team gives the three reasons “curiosity (aka fun), better understanding between humans and AI, and safety,” and provided some more detail:
Babies learn to talk without ever seeing a word written down. We wanted to see if a model could too. It can. It’s just very hard.
Speech is the most natural interface to any intelligence, super or otherwise, and today’s voice AI wastes it. It flattens what we say into text and can’t keep up with human timing.
AI keeps gaining power and independence, and it’s still nearly deaf to the emotion in our voices. Imagine being in serious pain while a voice AI has no idea and just keeps going. That’s the safety problem. Dessa is a step toward fixing it.
The Dessa team says it will be giving “a small group of AI safety researchers” early access to the model.

articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 23/10: Thế giới tăng cao, xăng trong nước 25.000 đồng/lít
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Giá dầu trên thị trường quốc tế trong phiên giao dịch 22/10 tăng mạnh, lên mức cao nhất 5 tháng.
Chốt phiên giao dịch 22/10, theo Reuters, giá dầu Brent tăng 4%, lên mức 113,2 USD/thùng, mức giá đóng cửa cao nhất kể từ ngày 4/5. Giá dầu WTI chốt phiên ở mức 99,47 USD/thùng, tăng 2,4%.
Tuy nhiên, đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay (23/10), giá dầu WTI đảo chiều đi xuống.
Theo dữ liệu từ Oilprice, vào lúc 7h03' ngày 23/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent vẫn được niêm yết ở mức 113,2 USD/thùng. Trong khi đó, giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh xuống mức 99,37 USD/thùng, giảm 0,1% so với phiên liền trước.
Giá dầu thế giới tăng mạnh trong bối cảnh căng thẳng tại Trung Đông gia tăng, làm dấy lên lo ngại về nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung năng lượng toàn cầu.
Theo giới phân tích, giá dầu tăng nhanh sau khi các cuộc tấn công của lực lượng Houthi tại Saudi Arabia gia tăng.
Ngày 21/10, lực lượng Houthi tại Yemen, nhóm được Iran hậu thuẫn, đã tiến hành các cuộc tấn công nhằm vào nhiều mục tiêu, trong đó có vụ tấn công bằng máy bay không người lái vào một mỏ dầu của Saudi Arabia.
Mỹ đã yêu cầu một số nhà ngoại giao cùng thân nhân rời khỏi các cơ quan đại diện của nước này tại Saudi Arabia.
Căng thẳng tiếp tục gia tăng khi truyền thông Iran đưa tin về các vụ nổ chưa rõ nguyên nhân tại khu vực Sirik ở miền nam nước này.
Bên cạnh đó, hoạt động vận tải dầu mỏ cũng đối mặt với nhiều rủi ro.
Theo dữ liệu từ Công ty phân tích dữ liệu Kpler, có ít nhất 18 vụ tấn công nhằm vào các tàu vận tải đã xảy ra trong hai tuần qua.
Các chuyên gia cảnh báo Iran đang nhắm mục tiêu vào các tàu chở dầu ở phạm vi xa hơn eo biển Hormuz, mở rộng tới Vịnh Oman. Việc này làm gia tăng nguy cơ gián đoạn hoạt động bốc xếp dầu thô tại khu vực Vịnh Oman cũng như hoạt động chuyển tải dầu giữa các tàu.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Tại thị trường trong nước, liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đã tiến hành điều chỉnh giá xăng dầu từ chiều qua (22/10).
Theo đó, ở kỳ điều hành 22/10, giá xăng dầu được điều chỉnh theo hướng xăng giảm, dầu diesel và mazut đều tăng so với kỳ điều hành liền trước.
Cụ thể, giá bán lẻ xăng E5RON92 không cao hơn 25.361 đồng/lít, giảm 1.610 đồng/lít so với kỳ trước.
Giá xăng E10RON95-III giảm 1.816 đồng/lít, giá bán không cao hơn 25.213 đồng/lít.
Ngược lại, giá dầu diesel 0.05S tăng 444 đồng/lít, lên mức tối đa 29.550 đồng/lít.
Giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S tăng 1.238 đồng/kg, có giá bán không cao hơn 23.373 đồng/kg.
Tại kỳ điều hành 22/10, cơ quan quản lý trích lập Quỹ Bình ổn giá xăng dầu đối với xăng sinh học ở mức 300 đồng/lít; không trích lập đối với dầu diesel và dầu mazut. Các mặt hàng đều không chi sử dụng quỹ.
Dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương cho thấy, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam đang ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Giá bán xăng dầu của các nước lân cận Việt Nam tính đến ngày 22/10 như sau:
Giá xăng tại Thái Lan là 32.941 đồng/lít (Chính phủ trợ giá); ở Campuchia là 32.010 đồng/lít (Chính phủ trợ giá); tại Lào là 48.276 đồng/lít; ở Trung Quốc là 35.017 đồng/lít (Chính phủ khống chế giá); Việt Nam có giá bán không cao hơn 25.213 đồng/lít.
Giá dầu tại Thái Lan là 34.117 đồng/lít (Chính phủ trợ giá); ở Campuchia là 35.179 đồng/lít; tại Lào là 40.848 đồng/lít; ở Trung Quốc là 31.924 đồng/lít (Chính phủ khống chế giá); Việt Nam giá bán không cao hơn 29.550 đồng/lít.

articles.title: Oracle pledges $1B over four years to partners that sell its AI tools
articles.text:
Oracle announced a $1B, four-year commitment to its partner ecosystem at AI World in Las Vegas, covering training, test and demo environments, cloud migration funding and Marketplace sales. It also changed Marketplace rules. The pledge comes as Oracle cuts costs to fund its AI data centres.
Oracle will spend $1B over the next four years on the companies that build, sell and install its software, the company said on Thursday. It made the pledge at its AI World conference in Las Vegas. The aim is to help partners cash in on demand for AI.
The money will go into Oracle’s partner programme. It covers training and certification, test and demo setups, funding to move customers onto Oracle’s cloud, and help selling through Oracle Marketplace, its online store for business software.
Partners include consulting firms, software makers, cloud providers and resellers. They build their own apps and AI agents on Oracle’s databases and cloud, or help customers set up and run Oracle software. In July, Oracle also put Google’s Gemini models into the tool its business-app customers use to build AI agents.
“Our partners extend our sales reach, expand our delivery capacity, and bring their own innovation and investment,” said Mark Hura, president of Oracle Global Field Operations.
Oracle also changed how its Marketplace works. Customers can now put more of their prepaid Oracle cloud credits toward partners’ products, and software makers can agree prices directly with buyers. Marketplace buying is also opening up in India and Japan.
The pledge is small next to Oracle’s AI spending. The company spent about $50B on capital projects in its last financial year and shed about 21,000 jobs as it moved money into cloud and AI data centres. In September, it set aside $700M more for job cuts it has yet to make.
In July, S&P cut Oracle’s credit rating to one notch above junk, citing the cash it is burning.
Oracle did not say how the $1B will be split, and said all benefits depend on its programme terms and eligibility rules.

articles.title: Tesla says it will no longer release the Cybertruck in Australia and New Zealand - Engadget
articles.text:
Tesla says it will no longer release the Cybertruck in Australia and New Zealand
It will be refunding people’s deposits.
Tesla won't be selling the Cybertruck in Australia and New Zealand, it told customers who reserved the vehicle seven years ago. In the email the automaker is sending out, it said that its "plans to produce Cybertruck" for those countries "have been discontinued." Because it can no longer fulfill orders for those regions, it will refund all deposits made by customers within 30 days after they receive the email confirming their details. Tesla is also giving them free year-long access to Full Self-Driving (Supervised) if they order a new Model 3 or Model Y.
According to Drive Australia, the Cybertruck's availaibility in its country had been in question for years. In 2023, when the automaker started delivering the vehicle to early buyers, the publication's sources said that Tesla's Texas factory wasn't configured to manufacture the Cybertruck in right-hand drive. Without a right-hand drive version, the Cybertruck can't be legally driven on the streets not just of Australia and New Zealand, but also of the UK, Japan and Ireland.
To note, Tesla hasn't officially released the Cybertruck in the UK and the European Union anyway, and the vehicle hasn't received any type of regulatory approval from European officials. It is believed that the model will not be approved in Europe, due to regulations related to crumple zones, pedestrian safety — it has a sharp edges that could strike people — lighting and weight classifications. Even the US Army couldn't import them into the region. "Several specifications of the Cybertruck, particularly the sharp-edged, stiff stainless-steel body, violate EU safety standards, primarily for the protection of vulnerable road users," the US Army Customs Agency said in a notification. If you've seen a Cybertruck in Europe, that's because customers have been able to secure single-vehicle approvals by making enough modifications.

articles.title: Soundcore’s latest noise-crushing headphones are on sale for a new low price
articles.text:
My colleague John Higgins considered Soundcore’s Space One some of the best budget noise-canceling headphones you could buy when they launched in 2023 — and their successor has only improved upon their winning formula, albeit with a $30 price increase. Thankfully, the Soundcore Space 2 are currently on sale at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart in all three colors for an all-time low of $106.49 ($23 off), making them even easier to recommend.
Soundcore’s latest noise-crushing headphones are on sale for a new low price
The Space 2 offer better ANC and sound over the original, making them an easy rec.
The Space 2 builds on the original with improved active noise cancellation, particularly when it comes to the low-frequency sounds associated with trains and airplane engines. They also deliver more accurate sound performance thanks to various design upgrades, while retaining many of the same features that made the Sound One sound so good for the price, including support for high-resolution LDAC audio. You also still get access to HearID 3.0, which lets you personalize the sound by listening to a series of samples and adjusting accordingly.
Battery life is another welcome improvement. The Space 2 can last up to 50 hours with ANC enabled or 70 hours with it switched off, up from 40 and 55 hours, respectively, on the original. And when your battery dies, you can still use the equipped 3.5mm jack for wired listening. They’ll also automatically pause playback when you take them off, which is handy when you need to step away without losing your place in a song or podcast.

articles.title: Oura sues Ultrahuman (again) to block its latest smart ring from the US market - Engadget
articles.text:
Oura sues Ultrahuman (again) to block its latest smart ring from the US market
It claims Ultrahuman's Ring Pro violates two separate patents, including a brand new one.
Last year, Oura successfully sued Ultrahuman and got a court to block sales of its Ring Air product in the US. Now, Oura has sued Ultrahuman again in a Texas federal court over its latest product, the Ring Pro, saying it violates two of its patents involving design and internal components, according to a Oura's blog post. Oura is seeking monetary damages and wants to (again) stop Ultrahuman from selling its latest wearable.
"After it was found to be infringing Oura patents, Ultrahuman recently introduced a modified version of its ring, claiming its redesign no longer infringed our patents. That claim is false. Ultrahuman's latest ring still incorporates many of Oura's patented innovations and continues to infringe our intellectual property," Oura claimed in the post.
India-based Ultrahuman's Ring Air was banned for sale in the US after the ITC ruled that it violated several Oura patents (it's still on sale in Europe and other markets). Ultrahuman subsequently redesigned its Ring Pro to avoid violating Oura's IP in America, and received approval from the US Customs and Border Protection earlier this year.
However, Finland-based Oura now says that Ultrahuman is violating two separate patents, including one that was approved just two days before the company filed its lawsuit, TechCrunch reported. That patent (12,769,363) appears to broadly cover a smart ring design with a housing, battery and specific internal components. The Ring Pro is manufactured at a plant in Plano, Texas for the US market by a company called SVTronics under Ultrahuman's direction, and Oura also named SVTronics as a defendant in the lawsuit.
Ultrahuman said it would fight Oura's legal action and that its Ring Pro remains on sale in the US. "The Ring Pro... redesign has already been through independent review in the United States: following an earlier patent proceeding, US Customs and Border Protection determined that Ring PRO did not infringe the Oura patent considered in that proceeding," an Ultrahuman spokesperson told Engadget in a statement. "Oura has now chosen to assert different patents, including one that issued just two days before this lawsuit was filed. We will address these claims through the appropriate legal process and will defend our position vigorously."
Oura has been in the press of late after it announced a partnership with the US military that included the use of a Palantir hosting environment. Last year, Samsung pre-emptively sued Oura in 2024 over concerns that Oura was itself planning to sue Samsung over its launch of the Galaxy Ring. Oura subsequently did sue Samsung, and as of this summer, the companies remain locked in a pitched legal battle over patents.
Update October 23, 7:53 AM ET: The article has been updated with Ultrahuman's statement to Engadget.

articles.title: Nscale sued in Norway over a data centre engineer's dismissal
articles.text:
An engineer at Nscale’s Stavanger data centre has sued the AI cloud firm and subcontractor CloudBrothers, Bloomberg reported. He claims Nscale directed his work like an employer and that he was fired after raising pay concerns. The case comes as Nscale prepares a contested IPO.
An engineer at Nscale’s data centre in Stavanger, Norway, has sued the British AI cloud company, claiming he was wrongly fired and hired through an illegal subcontracting setup, Bloomberg reported. The suit, backed by local trade unions, was filed on 16 October.
The engineer was employed through CloudBrothers, a subcontractor that is also named in the suit. He claims Nscale directed his daily work and shifts, which under Norwegian law would make it his real employer.
Norway allows subcontracting, but the subcontractor must manage its workers itself. If the client company treats them as its own staff, it must pay and treat them as full employees.
The engineer says he was fired in June after he pushed back on a CloudBrothers warning that staff who filed holiday requests late would lose two weeks of holiday pay. He replied to the whole team, according to the complaint:
“You cannot deduct our worked salary.”
He says he then contacted Norway’s labour inspection authority, and that CloudBrothers fired him in retaliation. CloudBrothers told him he was dismissed for repeated breaches of confidentiality, according to the filing. He is seeking compensation and a ruling that he should have been an Nscale employee.
Nscale and CloudBrothers did not immediately respond to Bloomberg’s requests for comment. Nscale had earlier told Bloomberg it cut ties in Stavanger with Technimove, the contractor that brought in workers through CloudBrothers.
The case comes as Nscale races to build data centres for more than $100B in contracts, most not yet earned, ahead of a New York stock market listing. Its flagship site in Glomfjord, Norway, is about six months late after cooling leaks and a fire, Bloomberg has reported.
Some investors have said Nscale’s target valuation of about $30B is too high, and Microsoft reportedly pulled out of its planned UK data centre this month. This week, Korea’s Elice fell 32% in its stock market debut as investors sold off firms that rent out AI computing power.
